questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: الصَّحَابِيَّةُ الْمَذْكُورُ زَوَاجُهَا فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The female companion whose marriage is noted in the Holy Qur'an

questions.question_arabic: مُنَظَّمَةُ الْعَمَلِ الدَّوْلِيَّةِ (ILO) تَهْدِفُ إِلَى:
questions.question_english: The International Labour Organization (ILO) primarily aims to:

A.arabic: نَشْرِ الْعَدَالَةِ الِاجْتِمَاعِيَّةِ وَحِمَايَةِ حُقُوقِ الْعُمَّالِ
A.english: Promoting social justice and protecting workers' rights

D.arabic: دَعْمِ التَّعَاوُنِ الِاقْتِصَادِيِّ بَيْنَ دُوَلِ الْعَالَمِ

questions.correct_answer_text_arabic: نَشْرِ الْعَدَالَةِ الِاجْتِمَاعِيَّةِ وَحِمَايَةِ حُقُوقِ الْعُمَّالِ
questions.correct_answer_text_english: Promoting social justice and protecting workers' rights
questions.explanation_arabic: منظمة العمل الدولية وكالة تابعة للأمم المتحدة تأسست عام 1919م لتعزيز العدالة الاجتماعية ووضع معايير العمل الدولية.
questions.explanation_english: The International Labour Organization (founded 1919) sets international labour standards and promotes social justice.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَهْدَافُ مُنَظَّمَةِ الْعَمَلِ الدَّوْلِيَّةِ فِي تَعْزِيزِ الْعَدَالَةِ الِاجْتِمَاعِيَّةِ وَمَعَايِيرِ الْعَمَلِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Objectives of the International Labour Organization in promoting social justice and labor standards

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ شُعَرَاءِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ :
questions.question_english: Not among the Pre-Islamic (Jahili) poets:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ عَصْرِ الشَّاعِرِ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ عَنْ شُعَرَاءِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing the literary period of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah from Jahili poets

questions.question_arabic: عَاصِمَةُ عُمَانَ :
questions.question_english: The capital of Oman is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: عَاصِمَةُ سَلْطَنَةِ عُمَانَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The capital of the Sultanate of Oman

questions.question_arabic: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُم بِاللَّيْلِ وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُم بِالنَّهَارِ﴾، فِي كَلِمَةِ «جَرَحْتُم» فِي الْآيَةِ:
questions.question_english: In the Quranic verse "And He it is who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed (jarahtum) by day", the word 'jarahtum' exhibits:
questions.explanation_arabic: جرحتم هنا مجاز واستعارة عن ارتكاب الذنوب وكسب الآثام من الجوارح، وتتكامل مع طباق الليل والنهار.
questions.explanation_english: 'Jarahtum' is a metaphor (Majaz) meaning 'what you have committed/earned of deeds with your limbs', alongside the antithesis between night and day.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: الْبَلَاغَةُ فِي كَلِمَةِ «جَرَحْتُمْ» بِمَعْنَى اكْتَسَبْتُمْ مِنَ الذُّنُوبِ (مَجَازٌ / طِبَاقٌ بَيْنَ اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Rhetorical figure in 'jarahtum' (metaphorical acquisition / contextual antithesis)

questions.question_arabic: وُلِدَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ لَيْلَةَ مَاتَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ، وَقِيلَ فِيهِ: «أَيُّ حَقٍّ رُفِعَ وَأَيُّ بَاطِلٍ وُضِعَ»:
questions.question_english: Born in Madinah the night Caliph Umar ibn al-Khattab died, regarding whom it was said: 'What truth was raised up, and what vanity was born':
questions.explanation_arabic: ولد عمر بن أبي ربيعة المخزومي القرشي ليلة استشهاد عمر بن الخطاب سنة 23هـ فسمي باسمه واشتهر بالغزل الحضري.
questions.explanation_english: Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah was born on the night Caliph Umar was martyred in 23 AH, leading to the famous quote.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَارِيخُ مَوْلِدِ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ الْمُنَوَّرَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The birth date of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah in Madinah al-Munawwarah

questions.question_arabic: الْأُمَمُ الْمُتَّحِدَةُ (UN) مُنَظَّمَةٌ دَوْلِيَّةٌ تَشَكَّلَتْ فِي عَامِ:
questions.question_english: The United Nations (UN) is an international organization formed in the year:
questions.explanation_arabic: تأسست منظمة الأمم المتحدة في 24 أكتوبر 1945م في سان فرانسيسكو بعد انتهاء الحرب العالمية الثانية.
questions.explanation_english: The United Nations was established on October 24, 1945, following the end of World War II.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَارِيخُ تَأْسِيسِ هَيْئَةِ الْأُمَمِ الْمُتَّحِدَةِ (1945م)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Founding date of the United Nations (1945 CE)

questions.question_arabic: السَّيِّدَةُ الَّتِي أَطْلَقَ عَلَيْهَا الْكُتَّابُ الْمُعَاصِرُونَ لَقَبَ "أُمِّ الْمِصْرِيِّينَ" :
questions.question_english: The lady upon whom contemporary writers bestowed the title "Umm al-Misriyyin" (Mother of the Egyptians):
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ "أُمِّ الْمِصْرِيِّينَ" لِلسَّيِّدَةِ صَفِيَّةَ زَغْلُولَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The title 'Mother of the Egyptians' for Mrs. Safiyyah Zaghlul

questions.question_arabic: عَاصِمَةُ الدَّوْلَةِ الْعَبَّاسِيَّةِ:
questions.question_english: The historic capital city of the Abbasid Caliphate:
questions.explanation_arabic: اتخذ العباسيون بغداد عاصمة لهم منذ بناها الخليفة المنصور عام 145هـ وظلت حاضرة الخلافة حتى عام 656هـ.
questions.explanation_english: Baghdad served as the capital of the Abbasid Caliphate from its founding in 762 CE until the Mongol sack in 1258 CE.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَحْدِيدُ بَغْدَادَ عَاصِمَةً رَسْمِيَّةً لِلْخِلَافَةِ الْعَبَّاسِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying Baghdad as the official capital of the Abbasid Caliphate

questions.question_arabic: الْخَرْطُومُ هِيَ عَاصِمَةُ :
questions.question_english: Khartoum is the capital of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَحْدِيدُ عَاصِمَةِ جُمْهُورِيَّةِ السُّودَانِ (الْخَرْطُومُ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identification of the capital of Sudan (Khartoum)

questions.question_arabic: «إِذَا رَأَتْهُ قُرَيْشٌ قَالَ قَائِلُهَا / إِلَى مَكَارِمِ هَذَا يَنْتَهِي الْكَرَمُ»، قَالَهُ الشَّاعِرُ:
questions.question_english: Who is the poet of: 'When Quraysh behold him, their spokesman declares: to the noble traits of this man does all generosity reach its summit'?
questions.explanation_arabic: هذا البيت من ميمية الفرزدق الشهيرة في مدح الإمام علي زين العابدين بن الحسين بن علي بمكة أمام هشام بن عبد الملك.
questions.explanation_english: From Al-Farazdaq's famous Mimiyyah ode composed at the Kaaba praising Imam Ali Zayn al-Abidin.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ مِيمِيَّةِ الْمَدِيحِ لِآلِ الْبَيْتِ إِلَى الْفَرَزْدَقِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attributing the famous panegyric for the Prophet's family to Al-Farazdaq

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ شُعَرَاءِ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ :
questions.question_english: Among the Christian poets is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: شُعَرَاءُ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْأُمَوِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Christian poets in the Umayyad period

questions.question_arabic: أَشْهَرُ الْخُطَبَاءِ الْعَرَبِ:
questions.question_english: The most famous of Arab pre-Islamic orators:
questions.explanation_arabic: قس بن ساعدة الإيادي هو أشهر خطباء الجاهلية وحكيم من حكماء العرب وضرب به المثل في البلاغة والخطابة في سوق عكاظ.
questions.explanation_english: Quss ibn Sa'idah al-Iyadi is the most celebrated pre-Islamic orator, proverbial for his eloquence at the Ukaz market.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَكَانَةُ قُسِّ بْنِ سَاعِدَةَ الْإِيَادِيِّ كَأَشْهَرِ خُطَبَاءِ الْعَرَبِ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Prominence of Quss ibn Sa'idah al-Iyadi as the most famous Arab pre-Islamic orator

questions.question_arabic: "النَّقْدُ الْمَنْهَجِيُّ عِنْدَ الْعَرَبِ" هُوَ مِنْ تَأْلِيفِ :
questions.question_english: "Al-Naqd al-Manhaji 'inda al-Arab" (Systematic Criticism among the Arabs) is authored by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَلِّفُ كِتَابِ النَّقْدِ الْمَنْهَجِيِّ عِنْدَ الْعَرَبِ (مُحَمَّد مَنْدُور)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of the book 'Al-Naqd al-Manhaji 'inda al-Arab' (Muhammad Mandur)

questions.question_arabic: «أَلَسْتُمْ خَيْرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ الْمَطَايَا ... وَأَنْدَى الْعَالَمِينَ بُطُونَ رَاحِ»، قَالَهُ:
questions.question_english: "Are you not the best of all who have ever mounted beasts of burden, and the most generous in palms of hands?" Said by:
questions.explanation_arabic: عد النقاد هذا البيت من قصيدة جرير الميمية 'أتصحو أم فؤادك غير صاح' أمدح بيت قالته العرب في الخلفاء.
questions.explanation_english: This line by Jarir in praise of Caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan was acclaimed by classical critics as the supreme panegyric in Arabic.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ أَمْدَحِ بَيْتٍ قَالَتْهُ الْعَرَبُ إِلَى الشَّاعِرِ جَرِيرٍ فِي مَدْحِ عَبْدِ الْمَلِكِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the most complimentary verse in Arabic to Jarir in praise of Abd al-Malik

questions.question_arabic: شَاعِرٌ شَهِيرٌ يُلَقَّبُ بِـ «شَاعِرِ الْخَلِيفَةِ» أَوْ شَاعِرِ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ:
questions.question_english: A renowned poet nicknamed "The Caliph's Poet" (or the official court poet of the Umayyads):
questions.explanation_arabic: لقب الأخطل بشاعر بني أمية وشاعر الخليفة لشدة قربه من عبد الملك بن مروان وارتدائه الصليب في بلاط الخلافة الأموية بدمشق.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Akhtal was honored as 'The Poet of the Caliph' for his close companionship with Caliph Abd al-Malik.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ «شَاعِرِ الْخَلِيفَةِ وَشَاعِرِ بَنِي أُمَيَّةَ» لِلْأَخْطَلِ التَّغْلِبِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Sobriquet 'Poet of the Caliph' for al-Akhtal al-Taghlibi

questions.question_arabic: «إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ لَنُورٌ يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ ... مُهَنَّدٌ مِنْ سُيُوفِ اللَّهِ مَسْلُولُ» قَالَ هَذَا الشِّعْرَ:
questions.question_english: 'Indeed, the Messenger is a light whence illumination is sought, an unsheathed Indian sword of God's swords' — who said this?
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ إِنَّ الرَّسُولَ لَنُورٌ يُسْتَضَاءُ بِهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the verse 'Inna al-Rasula la-nurun yustada'u bihi'

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ وُلِدَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ الْمُنَوَّرَةِ لَيْلَةَ مَاتَ عُمَرُ بْنُ الْخَطَّابِ :
questions.question_english: The poet born in al-Madinah al-Munawwarah the night Umar ibn al-Khattab died is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: وِلَادَةُ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ لَيْلَةَ وَفَاةِ عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Birth of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah on the night of Umar ibn al-Khattab's death

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنَ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْأُمَوِيِّينَ :
questions.question_english: He is not among the Umayyad poets:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَحْدِيدُ الشَّاعِرِ الَّذِي لَيْسَ مِنَ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْأُمَوِيِّينَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the poet who is not among the Umayyad poets

questions.question_arabic: «رَهِينُ الْمَحْبِسَيْنِ» هُوَ لَقَبُ :
questions.question_english: 'Rahin al-Mahbisayn' (Prisoner of the Two Prisons: his blindness and his home) is the title of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ رَهِينِ الْمَحْبِسَيْنِ لِأَبِي الْعَلَاءِ الْمَعَرِّيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The title Rahin al-Mahbisayn given to Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri

questions.question_arabic: «نَاقِدُ الْإِخْلَاصِ، هَزِيلُ الْعَقِيدَةِ الدِّينِيَّةِ وَالسِّيَاسِيَّةِ، شَدِيدُ التَّعَصُّبِ لِقَوْمِهِ»، قِيلَ هَذَا فِي وَصْفِ الشَّاعِرِ:
questions.question_english: "Lacking sincerity, of frail religious and political devotion, fiercely partisan to his tribe." This critical description was given of:
questions.explanation_arabic: وصف مؤرخو الأدب كالدكتور شوقي ضيف الأخطل بأنه كان مرتزقاً في بلاط بني أمية، ولم تكن له عقيدة سياسية سوى نصرة قبيلته بني تغلب.
questions.explanation_english: Literary historians characterized al-Akhtal as a consummate court mercenary whose only genuine loyalty was to his tribe, Banu Taghlib.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: التَّحْلِيلُ النَّقْدِيُّ لِشَخْصِيَّةِ الْأَخْطَلِ وَتَعَصُّبِهِ الْمُطْلَقِ لِقَوْمِهِ بَنِي تَغْلِبَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Critical analysis of al-Akhtal's tribal fanaticism for Banu Taghlib

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ هُوَ مَجْنُونُ لَيْلَى:
questions.question_english: Who is Majnun Layla?
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: الِاسْمُ الْحَقِيقِيُّ لِمَجْنُونِ لَيْلَى
questions.question_micro_focus_english: True name of Majnun Layla

questions.question_arabic: أَدِيبٌ لُبْنَانِيٌّ، مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِهِ تَارِيخُ التَّمَدُّنِ الْإِسْلَامِيِّ :
questions.question_english: A Lebanese literary figure and historian, author of 'Tarikh al-Tamaddun al-Islami':
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَلِّفُ تَارِيخِ التَّمَدُّنِ الْإِسْلَامِيِّ (جُرْجِي زَيْدَانَ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of Tarikh al-Tamaddun al-Islami (Jurji Zaydan)

questions.question_arabic: «اعْتَبِرُوا عِبَادَ اللَّهِ بِمَنْ مَاتَ مِنْكُمْ، وَتَفَكَّرُوا فِيمَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ أَيْنَ كَانُوا أَمْسِ وَأَيْنَ هُمُ الْيَوْمَ ؟»، قَالَهُ :
questions.question_english: 'Take heed, O servants of Allah, from those among you who have died, and reflect on those who were before you: where were they yesterday and where are they today?' was said in a sermon by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: خُطْبَةُ أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ فِي الْمَوْعِظَةِ وَالِاعْتِبَارِ بِالْمَوْتِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq's sermon on taking heed and reflecting on mortality

questions.question_arabic: «أَلَسْتُمْ خَيْرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ الْمَطَايَا ... وَأَنْدَى الْعَالَمِينَ بُطُونَ رَاحِ» قَالَ جَرِيرٌ هَذَا الشِّعْرَ فِي مَدْحِ:
questions.question_english: 'Are you not the best of those who ever mounted beasts, and the most generous of mankind in palm of hand?' — Jarir composed this in praise of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَمْدُوحُ جَرِيرٍ فِي بَيْتِ أَلَسْتُمْ خَيْرَ مَنْ رَكِبَ الْمَطَايَا
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Jarir's praise of Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan

questions.question_arabic:
«وَقَدْ أَغْتَدِي وَالطَّيْرُ فِي وُكُنَاتِهَا *** بِمُنْجَرِدٍ قَيْدِ الْأَوَابِدِ هَيْكَلِ»
فِي هَذَا الشِّعْرِ اسْتَخْدَمَ امْرُؤُ الْقَيْسِ لَفْظَ "مُنْجَرِدٍ" فِي مَعْنَى :
questions.question_english: In the verse: 'And often I go forth early in the morning while the birds are still in their nests, upon a short-haired steed that holds wild animals captive, massive in frame.' In this poetry, Imru' al-Qais used the word 'Munjared' (مُنْجَرِد) in the meaning of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْنَى كَلِمَةِ «مُنْجَرِدٍ» فِي مُعَلَّقَةِ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Meaning of the word 'Munjared' in Imru' al-Qais's Mu'allaqah

questions.question_arabic: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ لَا تَسْتَطِيعُ دَفْعَ مَنِيَّتِي فَدَعْنِي أُبَادِرْهَا بِمَا مَلَكَتْ يَدِي، قَالَهُ :
questions.question_english: "If you cannot avert my impending death, then let me anticipate it with what my wealth affords," spoken by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتٍ مِنْ مُعَلَّقَةِ طَرَفَةَ بْنِ الْعَبْدِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of a verse from Tarafah ibn al-Abd's Mu'allaqah

questions.question_arabic: «نَهْجُ الْبَلَاغَةِ» لِلْإِمَامِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ :
questions.question_english: 'Nahj al-Balaghah' attributed to Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (compiled by Al-Sharif al-Radi) is:

options_english.D: Collection of his sermons, letters, and maxims

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُحْتَوَى كِتَابِ «نَهْجِ الْبَلَاغَةِ» مِنْ خُطَبِ وَرَسَائِلِ وَحِكَمِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ أَبِي طَالِبٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Contents of Nahj al-Balaghah containing sermons and wisdom of Ali

questions.question_arabic: قَائِدٌ مُسْلِمٌ كَانَ مِنَ الْبَرْبَرِ وَمَوْلًى لِمُوسَى بْنِ نُصَيْرٍ، فَتَحَ الْأَنْدَلُسَ عَامَ 92هـ:
questions.question_english: A Muslim commander of Berber origin and lieutenant of Musa ibn Nusayr who conquered Al-Andalus in 92 AH:
questions.explanation_arabic: طارق بن زياد فتح الأندلس وهزم ملك القوط لذريق في معركة وادي لكة ونُسب إليه جبل طارق.
questions.explanation_english: Tariq ibn Ziyad led the Muslim crossing into Hispania in 711 CE (92 AH), giving his name to Gibraltar (Jabal Tariq).
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قِيَادَةُ طَارِقِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ لِفَتْحِ الْأَنْدَلُسِ وَخُطْبَتُهُ الْحَمَاسِيَّةُ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Tariq ibn Ziyad's leadership in the conquest of Al-Andalus and his martial speech

questions.question_arabic: أَشْعَرُ شُعَرَاءِ الْمُعَلَّقَاتِ هُمْ ثَلَاثَةٌ وَقَدْ أَجْمَعُوا تَقْرِيبًا عَلَى تَفْضِيلِهِمْ:
questions.question_english: The most poetic of the Mu'allaqat poets are three, almost unanimously favored:

options_arabic.A: امْرُؤُ الْقَيْسِ وَطَرَفَةُ بْنُ الْعَبْدِ وَالْحُطَيْئَةُ
options_arabic.B: امْرُؤُ الْقَيْسِ وَزُهَيْرُ بْنُ أَبِي سُلْمَى وَالنَّابِغَةُ الذُّبْيَانِيُّ

options_english.A: Imru' al-Qais, Tarafah ibn al-Abd, and al-Hutay'ah
options_english.B: Imru' al-Qais, Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, and al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَشْعَرُ شُعَرَاءِ الْمُعَلَّقَاتِ وَالْجَاهِلِيَّةِ (امْرُؤُ الْقَيْسِ وَزُهَيْرٌ وَالنَّابِغَةُ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Consensus ranking of the top three pre-Islamic poets

questions.question_arabic: قِيلَ لَهُ: «أَنْتَ أَشْجَعُ النَّاسِ وَأَشَدُّهُمْ». فَقَالَ: «لَا». قَالَ: «فَبِمَاذَا شَاعَ لَكَ ذَلِكَ؟» قَالَ: «كُنْتُ أُقْدِمُ إِذَا رَأَيْتُ الْإِقْدَامَ، وَأُحْجِمُ إِذَا رَأَيْتُ الْإِحْجَامَ، وَلَا أَدْخُلُ مَوْضِعًا لَا أَرَى لِي مِنْهُ مَخْرَجًا». قِيلَ فِي:
questions.question_english: 'You are the bravest and fiercest of men.' He said 'No... I would advance when I saw an opportunity to advance, and hold back when I saw reason to hold back, and never entered a place without seeing a way out.' Said of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: حِكْمَةُ وَشَجَاعَةُ الْفَارِسِ الشَّاعِرِ عَنْتَرَةَ بْنِ شَدَّادٍ فِي خَوْضِ الْمَعَارِكِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Antarah ibn Shaddad's wisdom and tactical bravery in battle

questions.question_arabic: يُسَمَّى عَرَبُ الشَّمَالِ :
questions.question_english: The Arabs of the North are called:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَسْمِيَةُ عَرَبِ الشَّمَالِ بِالْعَدْنَانِيِّينَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Designation of Northern Arabs as Adnanites

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ قَائِلُ: «أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، أَيْنَ الْمَفَرُّ؟ الْبَحْرُ مِنْ وَرَائِكُمْ، وَالْعَدُوُّ أَمَامَكُمْ، وَلَيْسَ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهِ إِلَّا الصِّدْقُ وَالصَّبْرُ»:
questions.question_english: Who is the orator of: 'O people, whither can you flee? The sea is behind you, and the enemy is before you, and by God you have nothing but truthfulness and steadfastness'?
questions.explanation_arabic: خطبة طارق بن زياد الشهيرة لجيشه عند جبل طارق قبل خوض معركة وادي لكة لفتح الأندلس.
questions.explanation_english: Tariq ibn Ziyad's iconic military speech rallying his soldiers on the shores of Andalusia before the battle.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ خُطْبَةِ الْحَثِّ عَلَى الْجِهَادِ عِنْدَ فَتْحِ الْأَنْدَلُسِ إِلَى طَارِقِ بْنِ زِيَادٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attributing the famous exhortation to battle upon entering Al-Andalus to Tariq ibn Ziyad

questions.question_arabic: «إِذَا بَلَغَ الْفِطَامَ لَنَا صَبِيٌّ تَخِرُّ لَهُ الْجَبَابِرُ سَاجِدِينَا»، قَالَهُ :
questions.question_english: "When a child among us reaches weaning, the tyrants fall prostrating before him," was said by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ مُعَلَّقَةِ عَمْرِو بْنِ كُلْثُومٍ فِي الْفَخْرِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the proud boast verse from the Mu'allaqah of Amr ibn Kulthum

questions.question_arabic: انْضَمَّ الْحَجَّاجُ إِلَى جَيْشٍ قَادَهُ:
questions.question_english: Al-Hajjaj initially joined the military under the command of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: بِدَايَةُ خِدْمَةِ الْحَجَّاجِ الْعَسْكَرِيَّةِ تَحْتَ رَوْحِ بْنِ زِنْبَاعٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Hajjaj's early service under Rawh ibn Zinba'

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ تَحَدَّثَ فِي شِعْرِهِ عَنْ حُرُوبِ دَاحِسَ وَالْغَبْرَاءِ وَمَدَحَ السَّاعِيَيْنِ فِي الصُّلْحِ:
questions.question_english: Who spoke in his poetry about the War of Dahis and Ghabra, praising the peacemakers?
questions.explanation_arabic: خلد زهير بن أبي سلمى في معلقته مآثر هرم بن سنان والحارث بن عوف لتحملهما ديات القتلى وإنهاء حرب داحس والغبراء.
questions.explanation_english: Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma praised Harim ibn Sinan and Al-Harith ibn Awf for paying blood-money to end the Dahis-Ghabra war.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَدْحُ زُهَيْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلْمَى لِمُصْلِحَيْ حَرْبِ دَاحِسَ وَالْغَبْرَاءِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma's praise for the peacemakers of the Dahis and Ghabra war

questions.question_arabic: لِمَاذَا ضَعُفَتِ الْخَطَابَةُ السِّيَاسِيَّةُ وَالْحَفْلِيَّةُ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْعَبَّاسِيِّ؟
questions.question_english: Why did political and celebratory oratory decline in the Abbasid era?

options_arabic.D: عَدَمُ وُجُودِ الْخُطَبَاءِ الْكِبَارِ فِي هَذَا الْعَصْرِ

options_english.C: Erection of veils/barriers between the Caliph and subjects
options_english.D: Absence of major orators in that era

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَسْبَابُ ضَعْفِ الْخَطَابَةِ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْعَبَّاسِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Reasons for the decline of political oratory during the Abbasid era

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ زُعَمَاءِ تَغْلِبَ، شَاعِرٌ جَاهِلِيٌّ نَصْرَانِيٌّ مِنْ شُعَرَاءِ الْمُعَلَّقَاتِ:
questions.question_english: A leader of Banu Taghlib, a pre-Islamic Christian poet among the Mu'allaqat authors:
questions.explanation_arabic: عمرو بن كلثوم التغلبي سيد قبيلة تغلب وفارسها صاحب المعلقة الفخرية الحماسية المشهورة.
questions.explanation_english: Amr ibn Kulthum was the paramount chieftain of Christian Banu Taghlib and composer of the heroic Mu'allaqah.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَرْجَمَةُ عَمْرِو بْنِ كُلْثُومٍ سَيِّدِ تَغْلِبَ وَصَاحِبِ الْمُعَلَّقَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Biography of Amr ibn Kulthum, chieftain of Taghlib and Mu'allaqah poet

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ كِبَارِ الْمُحَدِّثِينَ الْهُنُودِ :
questions.question_english: Among the greatest Hadith scholars and revivers of Islamic sciences in India:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: إِمَامُ الْمُحَدِّثِينَ وَالْمُجَدِّدُ الْأَكْبَرُ فِي الْهِنْدِ (الشَّاهُ وَلِيُّ اللَّهِ الدِّهْلَوِيُّ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Leader of Hadith scholars and greatest reviver in India (Shah Waliullah al-Dihlawi)

questions.question_arabic: هُوَ وَارِثُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي الْأَدَبِ وَالْبَلَاغَةِ :
questions.question_english: He is the heir of the Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) in literature and eloquence:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: وَارِثُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي الْبَلَاغَةِ (عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The heir of the Prophet in eloquence and literature (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ أَلْقَى «الْخُطْبَةَ الْبَتْرَاءَ»:
questions.question_english: Who delivered the famous historical oration known as "Al-Khutbah al-Batra'":
questions.explanation_arabic: ألقى زياد بن أبيه خطبته الشهيرة في البصرة عام 45 هـ وسميت 'البتراء' لأنه لم يبدأها بحمد الله والثناء عليه.
questions.explanation_english: Ziyad ibn Abihi delivered 'Al-Khutbah al-Batra'' upon his appointment to Basra, so named because he commenced without the customary praise of God.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ «الْخُطْبَةِ الْبَتْرَاءِ» الشَّهِيرَةِ إِلَى وَالِي الْبَصْرَةِ زِيَادِ بْنِ أَبِيهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the famous 'Khutbah Batra'' to Ziyad ibn Abihi

questions.question_arabic: الْمُوَشَّحُ ضَرْبٌ مِنَ الشِّعْرِ :
questions.question_english: Al-Muwashshah is a poetic genre in which:

options_arabic.A: لَا يُتَقَيَّدُ فِيهِ بِقَافِيَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَقَطْ

options_english.A: The poet is not restricted to a single rhyme scheme alone (varied rhymes/strophic)
options_english.B: The poet is restricted to one single rhyme only

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَعَدُّدُ الْقَوَافِي وَعَدَمُ التَّقَيُّدِ بِقَافِيَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فِي الْمُوَشَّحِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Variation of rhymes in the Andalusian Muwashshah

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ أَجْزَاءِ الْمُوَشَّحِ :
questions.question_english: Which of the following is NOT one of the specific constituent parts of the Andalusian Muwashshah?

options_arabic.C: الْقَافِيَةُ (مُصْطَلَحٌ عَامٌّ لَيْسَ جُزْءاً بِنَائِيّاً خَاصّاً كَالْقُفْلِ وَالْخَرْجَةِ)

options_english.C: Al-Qafiyah (General rhyme term, not specific structural unit like Simt, Dawr, Ghusn, Kharjah)

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَرْكَانُ وَأَجْزَاءُ الْمُوَشَّحِ الْأَنْدَلُسِيِّ وَاسْتِبْعَادُ الْقَافِيَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Components of the Andalusian Muwashshah and excluding general rhyme

questions.question_arabic: مُؤَلِّفُ حَيِّ بْنِ يَقْظَانَ:
questions.question_english: The author of 'Hayy ibn Yaqzan' is:
questions.explanation_arabic: رواية حي بن يقظان الفلسفية الشهيرة من تأليف الفيلسوف والأديب الأندلسي أبي بكر محمد بن عبد الملك بن طفيل القيسي.
questions.explanation_english: Hayy ibn Yaqzan is an allegory written by the Andalusian philosopher and writer Ibn Tufayl.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَلِّفُ رِسَالَةِ حَيِّ بْنِ يَقْظَانَ الْفَلْسَفِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The author of the philosophical treatise Hayy ibn Yaqzan

questions.question_arabic: طَابِقِ الْقَائِمَةَ I (الْأَعْلَامَ الْأَنْدَلُسِيِّينَ) مَعَ الْقَائِمَةِ II (الْمُؤَلَّفَاتِ):
questions.question_english: Match List I (Andalusian Authors) with List II (Their Literary Works):
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُطَابَقَةُ أَعْلَامِ النَّثْرِ الْأَنْدَلُسِيِّ مَعَ أَهَمِّ مُؤَلَّفَاتِهِمْ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Matching prominent Andalusian prose writers with their key works

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنَ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْأَنْدَلُسِيِّينَ :
questions.question_english: Not among the Andalusian poets:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ الشَّاعِرِ غَيْرِ الْأَنْدَلُسِيِّ (أَبُو الْعَلَاءِ الْمَعَرِّيُّ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing the non-Andalusian poet (Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri)

questions.question_arabic: مَنِ الَّذِي لُقِّبَ بِـ «مُتَنَبِّي الْغَرْبِ» بَيْنَ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْمَذْكُورِينَ أَدْنَاهُ؟
questions.question_english: Who among the following poets was titled 'Mutanabbi of the West' (Mutanabbi al-Gharb):
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَلْقِيبُ ابْنِ هَانِئٍ الْأَنْدَلُسِيِّ بِمُتَنَبِّي الْغَرْبِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Ibn Hani al-Andalusi titled as Mutanabbi of the West

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ جُبْرَانَ خَلِيل جُبْرَانَ :
questions.question_english: Not among the works of Jubran Khalil Jubran is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ جُبْرَانَ خَلِيل جُبْرَانَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing the works of Jubran Khalil Jubran

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ جِبْرَان خَلِيل جِبْرَان:
questions.question_english: Not among the works of Kahlil Gibran:

A.english: Dam'ah wa Ibtisamah (A Tear and a Smile)

questions.explanation_arabic: كتب جبران: «دمعة وابتسامة»، «النبي»، «الأجنحة المتكسرة»، «الأرواح المتمردة»؛ أما «الأرواح الحائرة» فليس من مؤلفاته.
questions.explanation_english: Kahlil Gibran wrote 'A Tear and a Smile', 'The Broken Wings', 'Spirits Rebellious', and 'The Prophet'; 'Al-Arwah al-Ha'irah' is not his.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ جِبْرَان خَلِيل جِبْرَان الْأَدَبِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing the literary works of Kahlil Gibran

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ جُبْرَانَ :
questions.question_english: It is NOT among the works of Jubran Khalil Jubran:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ الْكِتَابِ الَّذِي لَيْسَ مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ جُبْرَانَ خَلِيلِ جُبْرَانَ (الْأَرْوَاحُ الْحَائِرَةُ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing the book not authored by Jubran Khalil Jubran (Al-Arwah al-Ha'irah)

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ خَلِيل جِبْرَان:
questions.question_english: Not among the works of Kahlil Gibran:
questions.explanation_arabic: مؤلفات جبران تضم: الأرواح المتمردة، الأجنحة المتكسرة، دمعة وابتسامة، النبي، العواصف، المجنون؛ ولا يوجد له كتاب باسم «الأرواح الحائرة».
questions.explanation_english: Gibran's authentic oeuvre includes Spirits Rebellious, The Broken Wings, and The Prophet; 'Al-Arwah al-Ha'irah' is spurious.

questions.context_paragraph_arabic: «لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ الْأَبُ أَنْ يَحْمِلَ بَيْنَ جَانِحَتَيْهِ لِطِفْلِهِ الصَّغِيرِ عَوَاطِفَ الْأُمِّ فَهِيَ الَّتِي تَحُوطُهُ بِعِنَايَتِهَا وَرِعَايَتِهَا، وَتَبْسُطُ عَلَيْهِ جَنَاحَ رَحْمَتِهَا وَرَأْفَتِهَا، وَتَسْكُبُ قَلْبَهَا فِي قَلْبِهِ حَتَّى يَسْتَحِيلَا إِلَى قَلْبٍ وَاحِدٍ، يَخْفِقُ خُفُوقًا وَاحِدًا وَيَشْعُرُ بِشُعُورٍ وَاحِدٍ، وَهِيَ الَّتِي تَسْهَرُ عَلَيْهِ لَيْلَهَا وَتَكْلَؤُهُ نَهَارَهَا، وَتَحْتَمِلُ جَمِيعَ آلَامِ الْحَيَاةِ وَأَرْزَائِهَا فِي سَبِيلِهِ غَيْرَ شَاكِيَةٍ وَلَا مُتَبَرِّمَةٍ. وَلَوْ شِئْتُ أَنْ أَقُولَ لَقُلْتُ: إِنَّ سِرَّ الْحَيَاةِ الْإِنْسَانِيَّةِ وَيَنْبُوعَ وُجُودِهَا وَكَوْكَبَهَا الْأَعْلَى الَّذِي تَنْبَعِثُ مِنْهُ جَمِيعُ أَشِعَّتِهَا يَنْحَطُّ فِي كَلِمَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ هِيَ قَلْبُ الْأُمِّ. لَا يَسْتَطِيعُ الرَّجُلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ رَجُلًا حَتَّى يَجِدَ إِلَى جَانِبِهِ زَوْجَةً تَبْعَثُ فِي نَفْسِهِ رُوحَ الشَّجَاعَةِ وَالْهِمَّةِ وَتَغْرِسُ فِي قَلْبِهِ كِبْرِيَاءَ التَّبِعَةِ وَعَظَمَتَهَا، وَحَسْبُ الْمَرْءِ أَنْ يَعْلَمَ أَنَّهُ سَيِّدٌ وَأَنَّ رَعِيَّةً كَبِيرَةً أَوْ صَغِيرَةً تَضَعُ ثِقَتَهَا فِيهِ، وَتَسْتَظِلُّ بِظِلِّ حِمَايَتِهِ وَرِعَايَتِهِ، وَتَعْمِدُ فِي شُؤُونِ حَيَاتِهَا عَلَيْهِ حَتَّى يَشْعُرَ بِحَاجَتِهِ إِلَى اسْتِكْمَالِ جَمِيعِ صِفَاتِ السَّيِّدِ وَمَزَايَاهُ فِي نَفْسِهِ، فَلَا يَزَالُ يُعَالِجُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ نَفْسِهِ وَيَأْخُذُهَا بِهِ أَخْذًا حَتَّى يَتِمَّ لَهُ مَا يُرِيدُ. وَلَا يَسْتَطِيعُ الشَّيْخُ الْفَانِي أَنْ يَجِدَ فِي أُخْرَيَاتِ أَيَّامِهِ فِي قَلْبِ وَلَدِهِ الْفَتَى مِنَ الْحَنَانِ وَالْعَطْفِ وَالْحُبِّ وَالْإِيثَارِ، مَا يَجِدُ فِي قَلْبِ ابْنَتِهِ الْفَتَاةِ، فَهِيَ الَّتِي تَمْنَحُهُ يَدَهَا عُكَّازًا لِشَيْخُوخَتِهِ وَقَلْبَهَا مُسْتَوْدَعًا لِأَسْرَارِهِ كُلِّهِ تَتَسَمَّعُ أَنْفَاسَهُ، وَتُصْغِي إِلَى أَنَّاتِهِ، وَتَحْرِصُ الْحِرْصَ كُلَّهُ عَلَى أَنْ تَفْهَمَ مِنْ حَرَكَاتِ يَدَيْهِ، وَنَظَرَاتِ عَيْنَيْهِ حَاجَاتِهِ وَأَغْرَاضَهُ فَإِذَا نَزَلَ بِهِ قَضَاءُ اللَّهِ كَانَتْ هِيَ مِنْ دُونِ وَرَثَتِهِ جَمِيعًا الْوَارِثَةَ الْوَحِيدَةَ الَّتِي تَعُدُّ مَوْتَهُ نَكْبَةً عُظْمَى لَا يُهَوِّنُهَا عَلَيْهَا، وَلَا يُخَفِّفُ مِنْ لَوْعَتِهَا فِي نَفْسِهِ أَنَّهُ قَدْ تَرَكَ مِنْ بَعْدِهِ مِيرَاثًا عَظِيمًا، وَكَثِيرًا مَا سَمِعَ السَّامِعُونَ فِي بَيْتِ الْمَيِّتِ قَبْلَ أَنْ يَجِفَّ تُرَابُ قَبْرِهِ أَصْوَاتَ أَوْلَادِهِ يَتَجَادَلُونَ وَيَشْتَجِرُونَ فِي السَّاعَةِ الَّتِي يَجْتَمِعُ فِيهَا بَنَاتُهُ وَنِسَاؤُهُ فِي حُجُرَاتِهِنَّ نَائِحَاتٍ بَاكِيَاتٍ.»
questions.context_paragraph_english: "A father cannot carry in his bosom for his little child the sentiments of a mother; for it is she who envelops him with her care and protection, extends over him the wing of her mercy and tender affection, and pours her heart into his until they become a single heart, beating with one pulse and feeling with one emotion. She watches over him through the night and guards him through the day, bearing all of life's pains and hardships for his sake without complaint or vexation. If I were to state it, I would say: the secret of human life, the spring of its existence, and its loftiest star from which all its rays emanate is encapsulated in one phrase: the mother's heart. A man cannot become a true man until he finds beside him a wife who inspires in him the spirit of courage and resolve and implants in his heart the dignity and greatness of responsibility... Nor can the elderly father at the end of his days find in the heart of his young son the tenderness, compassion, love, and altruism that he finds in the heart of his young daughter; for she is the one who extends her hand as a walking stick for his old age and her heart as a repository for all his secrets... And when the decree of God descends upon him, she alone among all his heirs regards his death as a monumental catastrophe that cannot be alleviated by any great inheritance he left behind..."

questions.question_arabic: مَا مَعْنَى كَلِمَةِ (مَآقِي) فِي الْبَيْتِ الْمَذْكُورِ : «بِنْتُمْ وَبِنَّا فَمَا ابْتَلَّتْ جَوَانِحُنَا - شَوْقًا إِلَيْكُمْ وَلَا جَفَّتْ مَآقِينَا»؟
questions.question_english: What is the meaning of the word 'Ma'aqi' in the verse 'You parted and we parted, yet our ribs never cooled from yearning for you, nor have our tear ducts/eyes dried':
questions.context_paragraph_arabic:
«أَضْحَى التَّنَائِي بَدِيلًا عَنْ تَدَانِينَا - وَنَابَ عَنْ طِيبِ لُقْيَانَا تَجَافِينَا
بِنْتُمْ وَبِنَّا فَمَا ابْتَلَّتْ جَوَانِحُنَا - شَوْقًا إِلَيْكُمْ وَلَا جَفَّتْ مَآقِينَا
يَكَادُ حِينَ تُنَاجِيكُمْ ضَمَائِرُنَا - يَقْضِي عَلَيْنَا الْأَسَى لَوْلَا تَأَسِّينَا
حَالَتْ لِبُعْدِكُمُ أَيَّامُنَا فَغَدَتْ - سُودًا وَكَانَتْ بِكُمْ بِيضًا لَيَالِينَا
لِيَسْقِ عَهْدَكُمُ عَهْدُ السُّرُورِ فَمَا - كُنْتُمْ لِأَرْوَاحِنَا إِلَّا رَيَاحِينَا»
questions.context_paragraph_english:
Parting has become a substitute for our closeness, and estrangement has replaced the sweetness of our meeting.
You departed and we departed, yet our ribs never cooled from longing for you, nor have our tear ducts dried.
When our innermost thoughts secretly converse with you, grief almost destroys us were it not for our comforting patience.
Our days have turned black because of your distance, whereas our nights through you used to be white.
May the time of your presence be watered with joy, for to our souls you were nothing but fragrant basil flowers.

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ قَرَضَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتِ:
questions.question_english: Who composed these verses ('Salamun alaykum rijala al-wafa...'):
questions.context_paragraph_arabic:
«سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ رِجَالَ الْوَفَاءِ ... وَأَلْفُ سَلَامٍ عَلَى الْوَافِيَاتِ
وَيَا فَرَحَ الْقَلْبِ بِالنَّاشِئِينَ ... فَفِي هَؤُلَاءِ عِلَاجُ الشَّكَاةِ
أَرَى فِيكُمُ كَوْكَبًا سَاطِعًا ... يُنِيرُ الدُّجَى لِجَمِيعِ السُّرَاةِ
تَقَدَّمْتُمُ أُمَمًا بِالْعُلُومِ ... وَبِالْمُبْتَكَرَاتِ وَبِالْمُعْجِزَاتِ
شَبَابَ الْبِلَادِ وَأَنْتُمْ حِمَاهَا ... وَحِصْنُ الْحِمَى فِي الْخُطُوبِ الْعُتَاةِ»
questions.context_paragraph_english:
Peace be upon you, men of loyalty, and a thousand greetings to the loyal women.
How the heart rejoices in the rising generation, for in them is the beauty of life.
They are the fortresses and walls of the country, the pride of its guards and protectors.
Tomorrow belongs to them and is made by them, so let yesterday boast of what is to come.
When I magnify the status of youth, it is because youth is the father of miracles.
And blessed are the mothers who give birth to genius men and genius women.
For how many a nation was immortalized by a pen (yara'), and how many a nation arose from an inkwell (dawat)!

questions.question_arabic: «وَالْخُبْزُ كَالْعَنْبَرِ الْهِنْدِيِّ عِنْدَهُمُ ... وَالْقَمْحُ خَمْسُونَ إِرْدَبّاً بِدِينَارِ»، قَالَهُ:
questions.question_english: "And bread to them is like Indian ambergris, while wheat is fifty ardabbs for a single dinar." Said by:
questions.explanation_arabic: البيت من قصيدة هجائية شهيرة للشاعر جرير يهجو فيها قوماً بالبخل الشديد وتقتير الطعام.
questions.explanation_english: This satirical line mocking extreme miserliness is from the Umayyad poet Jarir.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتٍ هِجَائِيٍّ طَرِيفٍ فِي وَصْفِ الْبُخْلِ إِلَى الشَّاعِرِ جَرِيرٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of a satirical verse describing stinginess to Jarir

questions.question_arabic: خَلِيفَةُ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ وَمِنَ الشُّعَرَاءِ :
questions.question_english: A Caliph for a single day and night, and one of the finest poets and critics:

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Ibn al-Mu'tazz reigning as Caliph for one day and poetic stature

questions.question_english: Who among the following was not a Pre-Islamic (Jahili) poet:
questions.explanation_arabic: عمر بن أبي ربيعة شاعر أموي قرشي رائد الغزل الصريح في العصر الأموي، بينما الباقون شعراء جاهليون.
questions.explanation_english: Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah was a prominent Umayyad poet of erotic ghazal, whereas the others were Pre-Islamic poets.

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah as an Umayyad urban love poet

questions.question_english: Which of the following is not among the works of Yaqut al-Hamawi:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ مَعَاجِمِ وَمُؤَلَّفَاتِ يَاقُوتَ الْحَمَوِيِّ عَنْ كِتَابِ بُغْيَةِ الْوُعَاةِ لِلسُّيُوطِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing Yaqut al-Hamawi's works from Bughyat al-Wu'ah

questions.question_arabic: قَبِيلَةٌ عَرَبِيَّةٌ مِنْ غَطَفَانَ مِنَ الْعَدْنَانِيَّةِ أُخْتُ عَبْسٍ كَانَتْ بَيْنَهُمَا حَرْبُ دَاحِسٍ وَالْغَبْرَاءِ :
questions.question_english: An Arab Adnanite tribe from Ghatafan, sister to Abs, between whom occurred the War of Dahis and al-Ghabra:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قَبِيلَةُ ذُبْيَانَ وَحَرْبُ دَاحِسٍ وَالْغَبْرَاءِ مَعَ عَبْسٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The tribe of Dhubyan and the War of Dahis and al-Ghabra with Abs

questions.question_arabic:
رَتِّبْ شُعَرَاءَ الْمَدِيحِ النَّبَوِيِّ فِيمَا أَدْنَاهُ وَفْقاً لِعُصُورِهِمْ مَعَ اسْتِخْدَامِ الشِّفْرَةِ التَّالِيَةِ:
(i) ابْنُ نُبَاتَةَ الْمِصْرِيُّ (ii) حَسَّانُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ (iii) أَحْمَد شَوْقِي (iv) الْبُوصِيرِيُّ
questions.question_english:
Arrange the poets of Prophetic Panegyric (Madih Nabawi) chronologically according to their eras:
(i) Ibn Nubatah al-Misri (ii) Hassan ibn Thabit (iii) Ahmad Shawqi (iv) Al-Busiri

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Arranging poets of Prophetic Panegyric across eras

questions.question_arabic: يُعْتَبَرُ الْحُطَيْئَةُ مِنْ كِبَارِ الشُّعَرَاءِ، امْتَازَ بِالْهِجَاءِ، أَدْرَكَ:

C.english: Early Islam and the Umayyad period

questions.explanation_english: Al-Hutay'ah lived in both the Pre-Islamic and Islamic eras, making him a Mukhadram poet.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَحْدِيدُ الْعَصْرَيْنِ اللَّذَيْنِ عَاشَ فِيهِمَا الشَّاعِرُ الْمُخَضْرَمُ الْحُطَيْئَةُ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the eras witnessed by the Mukhadram poet al-Hutay'ah

questions.question_english: Who among the following celebrated epistolographers served as a vizier:
questions.explanation_arabic: ابن العميد كان وزيراً لركن الدولة البويهي، ولقب بالأستاذ الرئيس، وكذلك الصاحب بن عباد والقاضي الفاضل.
questions.explanation_english: Ibn al-Amid (as well as al-Sahib ibn Abbad) was a celebrated master of epistolary prose who held the office of vizier under the Buyids.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ الْكُتَّابِ الَّذِينَ تَوَلَّوْا الْوِزَارَةَ كَابْنِ الْعَمِيدِ وَالصَّاحِبِ بْنِ عَبَّادٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the master prose stylists who attained the vizierate

questions.question_arabic: دَخَلَ الصَّحَابِيُّ وَالشَّاعِرُ حَسَّانُ بْنُ ثَابِتٍ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ وَكَانَ عُمْرُهُ:
questions.question_english: Hassan ibn Thabit embraced Islam at the age of:
questions.explanation_arabic: عاش حسان بن ثابت الأنصاري ستين سنة في الجاهلية شاعراً للغساسنة، وستين سنة في الإسلام شاعراً للرسول ﷺ ومات عن 120 عاماً.
questions.explanation_english: Hassan ibn Thabit spent sixty years in Pre-Islamic Arabia and sixty years in Islam, living to the age of 120.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: بُلُوغُ حَسَّانَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ سِنَّ السِّتِّينَ حِينَ دَخَلَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Hassan ibn Thabit entering Islam at age sixty

questions.question_english: Who among the following is not classified among the Brigand (Sa'alik) poets:
questions.explanation_arabic: الشنفرى وتأبط شراً من قادة الصعاليك؛ أما عنترة والمهلهل فكانا من فرسان القبائل وسادتها.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Shanfara and Ta'abbata Sharran were quintessential Sa'alik, while Antarah and al-Muhalhil were tribal warriors.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ الشُّعَرَاءِ الصَّعَالِيكِ كَالشَّنْفَرَى وَتَأَبَّطَ شَرّاً عَنْ فُرْسَانِ الْقَبَائِلِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing Sa'luk outlaws from tribal chieftains and knights like Antarah and al-Muhalhil

questions.question_english: Who used to compose praise poetry for both the Munadhirah and the Ghassanids?
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَدْحُ حَسَّانَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ لِمُلُوكِ الْغَسَاسِنَةِ وَالْمَنَاذِرَةِ قَبْلَ الْإِسْلَامِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Hassan ibn Thabit's praise of Ghassanid and Lakhmid rulers

questions.question_arabic: أَشْهَرُ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْعَبَّاسِيِّينَ اشْتُهِرَ بِخَمْرِيَّاتِهِ :
questions.question_english: The most famous Abbasid poet renowned for his wine poetry (khamriyyat) is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَشْهَرُ شُعَرَاءِ الْخَمْرِيَّاتِ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْعَبَّاسِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The most famous poet of wine poetry in the Abbasid period

(i) أَبُو نُوَاسٍ
(ii) ابْنُ الرُّومِيِّ

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Chronological death ordering of Bashshar, Abu Nuwas, Ibn al-Rumi, and al-Mutanabbi

questions.correct_answer_text_arabic: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ سُلَيْمَانَ
questions.correct_answer_text_english: Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Sulayman
questions.explanation_arabic: أبو العلاء المعري هو أحمد بن عبد الله بن سليمان القضاعي التنوخي المعري (رهين المحبسين).

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Full genealogical name of Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri al-Tanukhi

questions.question_english: A famous Arab historian who established a new methodology in historiography and sociology, influencing European historians; he is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: رِيَادَةُ ابْنِ خَلْدُونَ لِفَلْسَفَةِ التَّارِيخِ وَعِلْمِ الِاجْتِمَاعِ الْعُمْرَانِيِّ

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of the epitaph verse: 'This is what my father perpetrated against me' (Abu al-Ala al-Ma'arri)

questions.explanation_english: Bisharah al-Khuri was nicknamed 'Al-Akhtal al-Saghir' for the classical elegance and lyrical beauty of his verse.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ لَقَبِ «الْأَخْطَلِ الصَّغِيرِ» لِلشَّاعِرِ اللُّبْنَانِيِّ بِشَارَةَ الْخُورِي
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the poetic sobriquet 'Al-Akhtal al-Saghir' for Lebanese poet Bisharah al-Khuri

questions.question_arabic: كَمْ مَقَالَةً يَنْقَسِمُ فِيهَا كِتَابُ «الْفِهْرِسْتِ» لِابْنِ النَّدِيمِ:

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَقْسِيمُ كِتَابِ الْفِهْرِسْتِ لِابْنِ النَّدِيمِ إِلَى عَشْرِ مَقَالَاتٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The ten major thematic sections of al-Fihrist by Ibn al-Nadim

questions.question_arabic: أَلَّفَ هَذَا الشَّاعِرُ فِي مَعَانِي الْقُرْآنِ كِتَاباً لَهُ مَجْمُوعَةُ رَسَائِلَ وَ دِيوَانُ شِعْرٍ ثُمَّ كِتَابُ "نَهْجِ الْبَلَاغَةِ" :
questions.question_english: This poet authored a book on the meanings of the Qur'an, has a collection of epistles, a poetry Diwan, and compiled the book 'Nahj al-Balaghah':
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَلَّفَاتُ الشَّرِيفِ الرَّضِيِّ فِي الْقُرْآنِ وَالشِّعْرِ وَنَهْجِ الْبَلَاغَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Works of Al-Sharif al-Radi in Qur'anic meanings, poetry, and Nahj al-Balaghah

questions.question_arabic: «وَقَدْ وَلَدَتْهُ أُمُّهُ أَعْمَى فَمَا نَظَرَ إِلَى الدُّنْيَا قَطُّ»:
questions.question_english: His mother gave birth to him blind, and he never looked upon the world at all:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: وِلَادَةُ الشَّاعِرِ بَشَّارِ بْنِ بُرْدٍ ضَرِيرًا
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Bashshar ibn Burd's innate blindness from birth

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ شُعَرَاءِ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْأُمَوِيِّ:
questions.question_english: Among the Christian poets of the Umayyad era:
questions.explanation_arabic: غياث بن غوث التغلبي (الأخطل) كان نصرانياً وشاعر بني أمية المقرب من عبد الملك بن مروان.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Akhtal al-Taghlibi was an Arab Christian and the court poet of the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ الشَّاعِرِ النَّصْرَانِيِّ الْأَخْطَلِ التَّغْلِبِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing the Christian poet Al-Akhtal al-Taghlibi

questions.question_arabic: شَاعِرٌ بَغْدَادِيٌّ مِنْ كِبَارِ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْعَبَّاسِيِّينَ اشْتَهَرَ بِشِعْرِ الزُّهْدِ وَالْحِكْمَةِ:
questions.question_english: A Baghdadi poet among the great Abbasids, famed as the foremost poet of asceticism (Zuhd) and wisdom:
questions.explanation_arabic: أبو العتاهية إسماعيل بن القاسم إمام شعراء الزهد في بغداد في عهد المهدي وهارون الرشيد.
questions.explanation_english: Abu al-Atahiyah was the pre-eminent Abbasid poet of asceticism (Zuhdiyyat) and moral contemplation in Baghdad.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: رِيَادَةُ أَبِي الْعَتَاهِيَةِ فِي شِعْرِ الزُّهْدِ وَالْمَوَاعِظِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Abu al-Atahiyah's pioneering leadership in ascetic and homiletic verse

questions.question_arabic: الْفَرَزْدَقُ كَانَ مِنْ مُعَاصِرِي:
questions.question_english: Al-Farazdaq was a contemporary of:
questions.explanation_arabic: عاش الفرزدق وجرير في العصر الأموي واشتهرا بالمنافسة الشعرية والمهاجاة في فن النقائض.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Farazdaq and Jarir lived during the Umayyad era and are famously known for their mutual poetic rivalry.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُعَاصَرَةُ الْفَرَزْدَقِ لِجَرِيرٍ فِي شِعْرِ النَّقَائِضِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Farazdaq's contemporaneity with Jarir in Naqa'id poetry
