questions.question_english: "This is he whose footstep the valley of Mecca knows, and whom the Sacred House knows, the unhallowed land and the sanctuary." Said by:
questions.explanation_arabic: القصيدة ميمية الفرزدق الشهيرة التي ارتجلها في الحرم المكي مدحاً لزين العابدين علي بن الحسين بن علي رضي الله عنهم.
questions.explanation_english: This world-renowned ode was declaimed by al-Farazdaq in the sanctuary of Mecca praising Zayn al-Abidin.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ قَصِيدَةِ مَدْحِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ زَيْنِ الْعَابِدِينَ إِلَى الْفَرَزْدَقِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the ode praising Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin to al-Farazdaq

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الْعَبَّاسِيُّ الَّذِي رَافَقَهُ الْفَقْرُ وَالشُّؤْمُ فِي مُعْظَمِ أَيَّامِ حَيَاتِهِ:
questions.question_english: The Abbasid poet accompanied by chronic poverty, misfortune, and pessimism throughout most of his life:
questions.explanation_arabic: عاش ابن الرومي حياة بائسة مليئة بالفواجع وفقد الأحبة والفقر الشديد والتشاؤم المستمر حتى مات مسموماً.
questions.explanation_english: Ibn al-Rumi lived an intensely tragic life marked by poverty, bereavement, and deep-seated superstition.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ مَآسِي حَيَاةِ ابْنِ الرُّومِيِّ وَمُلَازَمَةِ الْفَقْرِ وَالتَّطَيُّرِ لَهُ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Knowing Ibn al-Rumi's tragic life characterized by poverty and extreme pessimism

questions.question_arabic: وُلِدَ الْحَرِيرِيُّ فِي مَدِينَةِ «مَشَانَ» وَهِيَ قَرِيبَةٌ مِنْ:
questions.question_english: Al-Hariri was born in the town of "Mashan", which is situated near:
questions.explanation_arabic: ولد أبو محمد القاسم بن علي الحريري في بلدة مشان من ضواحي البصرة بالعراق سنة 446 هـ.
questions.explanation_english: Abu Muhammad al-Qasim al-Hariri was born in Mashan, near Basra, Iraq, in 446 AH.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَسْقِطُ رَأْسِ الْحَرِيرِيِّ فِي مَشَانَ مِنْ ضَوَاحِي الْبَصْرَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Birthplace of al-Hariri in Mashan, a township near Basra

questions.question_arabic: الْكَاتِبُ وَالْأَدِيبُ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْعَبَّاسِيِّ الَّذِي كَانَ ذَا شَغَفٍ وَبَرَاعَةٍ بِفَنِّ الرَّسْمِ وَالتَّصْوِيرِ وَالْخَطِّ:
questions.question_english: The Abbasid writer, vizier, and scholar who was renowned for his passion and skill in painting, drawing, and calligraphy:
questions.explanation_arabic: كان ابن العميد بارعاً في الرسم والتصوير والنحت والخط العربي وتدبير الآلات والعلوم الرياضية إلى جانب كتابته.
questions.explanation_english: Ibn al-Amid was celebrated for his artistic talents in drawing, design, and calligraphy alongside his literary mastery.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: بَرَاعَةُ ابْنِ الْعَمِيدِ فِي فُنُونِ الرَّسْمِ وَالتَّصْوِيرِ وَالْخَطِّ إِلَى جَانِبِ الْكِتَابَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Ibn al-Amid's multifaceted genius in drawing, calligraphy, and epistolary prose

questions.question_arabic: «لَوْلَا شِعْرُهُ لَذَهَبَ ثُلُثُ لُغَةِ الْعَرَبِ وَنِصْفُ أَخْبَارِ النَّاسِ»، قِيلَ فِي:
questions.question_english: "Were it not for his poetry, a third of the Arabic language and half of Arab historical lore would have been lost." Said of:
questions.explanation_arabic: أجمع أئمة اللغة أن شعر الفرزدق كان المرجع الأساسي لرواية مفردات اللغة وأيام العرب وأخبار القبائل في الجاهلية والإسلام.
questions.explanation_english: Classical philologists regarded al-Farazdaq's vast poetic corpus as an indispensable repository of ancient Arabic vocabulary.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: شَهَادَةُ ابْنِ سَلَّامٍ وَأَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ فِي الْقِيمَةِ اللُّغَوِيَّةِ وَالتَّارِيخِيَّةِ الْفَرِيدَةِ لِشِعْرِ الْفَرَزْدَقِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Classical philological consensus on al-Farazdaq's linguistic preservation

questions.question_arabic: وُلِدَ الْقَاضِي الْفَاضِلُ بِمَدِينَةِ:
questions.question_english: Al-Qadi al-Fadil was born in the city of:
questions.explanation_arabic: ولد أبو علي عبد الرحيم بن علي البيساني العسقلاني (القاضي الفاضل) في عسقلان بفلسطين سنة 529 هـ.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Qadi al-Fadil was born in Ashkelon, Palestine, in 529 AH (1135 CE).
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَسْقِطُ رَأْسِ الْقَاضِي الْفَاضِلِ فِي مَدِينَةِ عَسْقَلَانَ بِفِلَسْطِينَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Birthplace of al-Qadi al-Fadil in Ashkelon, Palestine

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الَّذِي يُعْرَفُ بِـ «شَاعِرِ الْمُجْتَمَعِ» (شَاعِرِ الشَّعْبِ) لِاتِّصَالِهِ الْمُبَاشِرِ بِهِمُومِ النَّاسِ:
questions.question_english: The poet renowned as "Poet of Society / Poet of the People" for his direct engagement with the public:
questions.explanation_arabic: لقب حافظ إبراهيم بشاعر الشعب وشاعر النيل لأنه كان لسان حال الجماهير والمعبر الصادق عن آلامهم وتطلعاتهم.
questions.explanation_english: Hafiz Ibrahim was titled 'Poet of the Nile' and 'Poet of the People' because of his close identification with social issues.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ «شَاعِرِ النِّيلِ وَشَاعِرِ الشَّعْبِ وَالْمُجْتَمَعِ» لِحَافِظ إِبْرَاهِيم
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Sobriquet 'Poet of the People and Society' for Hafiz Ibrahim

questions.question_arabic: اسْمُ الشَّاعِرِ الْأُمَوِيِّ الَّذِي كَانَتْ كُنْيَتُهُ «أَبَا حَزْرَةَ»:
questions.question_english: The Umayyad master poet whose agnomen (kunya) was "Abu Hazrah":
questions.explanation_arabic: جرير بن عطية التميمي كنيته المشهورة أبو حزرة، وكنية الفرزدق أبو فراس، وكنية الأخطل أبو مالك.
questions.explanation_english: Jarir ibn Atiyyah's well-known kunya was Abu Hazrah (named after his eldest son Hazrah).
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ كُنْيَةِ الشَّاعِرِ جَرِيرٍ بِـ «أَبِي حَزْرَةَ» نِسْبَةً إِلَى ابْنِهِ حَزْرَةَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying Jarir's kunya as Abu Hazrah after his son Hazrah

questions.question_arabic: "مَا زَالَ هَذَا الْقُرَشِيُّ يَهْذِي حَتَّى قَالَ الشِّعْرَ" قَالَ جَرِيرٌ هَذَا الْمَقَالَ عَنْ :
questions.question_english: "This Qurashi kept babbling until he composed poetry" — Jarir said this statement about:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قَوْلُ جَرِيرٍ فِي الشَّاعِرِ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Jarir's statement regarding the poet Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah

questions.question_arabic: الطِّرِمَّاحُ بْنُ حَكِيمٍ يُعَدُّ مِنْ :
questions.question_english: Al-Tirimmāḥ ibn Ḥakīm is considered among:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَصْنِيفُ الطِّرِمَّاحِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ ضِمْنَ شُعَرَاءِ الْمُفَضَّلِيَّاتِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Classification of al-Tirimmah ibn Hakim among the poets of al-Mufaddaliyyat

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ هُوَ الشَّاعِرُ الْفِلَسْطِينِيُّ مِنَ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْمَذْكُورِينَ:
questions.question_english: Who among the following is the renowned Palestinian national poet:
questions.explanation_arabic: محمود درويش شاعر فلسطين الأكبر وأحد أبرز شعراء المقاومة العربية والرمز الوطني للشعر الفلسطيني المعاصر.
questions.explanation_english: Mahmoud Darwish is internationally celebrated as the national poet of Palestine and a titan of contemporary Arabic poetry.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَحْدِيدُ جِنْسِيَّةِ الشَّاعِرِ مَحْمُود دَرْوِيش كَشَاعِرِ الْقَضِيَّةِ الْفِلَسْطِينِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying Mahmoud Darwish as the preeminent poet of Palestine

questions.question_arabic: جَمِيلُ بْنُ مَعْمَرٍ (جَمِيلُ بُثَيْنَةَ) وُلِدَ فِي الْحِجَازِ وَمَاتَ فِي:
questions.question_english: Jamil ibn Ma'mar (Jamil Buthaynah) was born in the Hijaz and passed away in:
questions.explanation_arabic: وفد جميل بثينة العذري على والي مصر عبد العزيز بن مروان فأكرمه، وتوفي بمصر سنة 82 هـ ورثته حبيبته بثينة.
questions.explanation_english: Jamil ibn Ma'mar, the archetype of chaste Udhri love poetry, passed away in Egypt in 82 AH (701 CE).
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَوْطِنُ وَوَفَاةُ الشَّاعِرِ الْعُذْرِيِّ جَمِيلِ بْنِ مَعْمَرٍ بِمِصْرَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Death of the Udhri poet Jamil Buthaynah in Egypt

questions.question_arabic: هُوَ فَارِسِيُّ الْأَصْلِ، بَرَعَ فِي الْإِنْشَاءِ وَالتَّرَسُّلِ، لُقِّبَ بِـ «الْجَاحِظِ الثَّانِي»:
questions.question_english: He was of Persian ancestry, excelled in epistolary prose, and was titled "The Second Jahiz":
questions.explanation_arabic: أبو الفضل محمد بن العميد كاتب ووزير بني بويه لقب بالجاحظ الثاني لبلاغته وسعة معارفه.
questions.explanation_english: Abu al-Fadl ibn al-Amid was hailed as 'The Second Jahiz' for his encyclopedic knowledge and prose brilliance.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ «الْجَاحِظِ الثَّانِي» لِلْكَاتِبِ وَالْوَزِيرِ ابْنِ الْعَمِيدِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Title 'The Second Jahiz' for Ibn al-Amid

questions.question_arabic: «إِنَّ الرُّصَافَةَ مَنْزِلٌ لِخَلِيفَةٍ ... جَمَعَ الْمَكَارِمَ وَالْعَزَائِمَ وَالتُّقَى»، كَلِمَةُ «الْعَزَائِمِ» هِيَ جَمْعُ:
questions.question_english: In the verse on al-Rusafah: "Al-Rusafah is the dwelling of a Caliph who combined noble deeds, determination (Aza'im), and piety." The word 'Aza'im' is the plural of:
questions.explanation_arabic: العزائم على وزن فعائل، ومفردها عزيمة، ككريمة وكرائم.
questions.explanation_english: 'Aza'im' follows the measure 'Fa'a'il', whose singular form is 'Azimah'.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُفْرَدُ كَلِمَةِ «عَزَائِمَ» (عَزِيمَةٌ) صَرْفِيّاً
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Morphological singular of 'Aza'im' as 'Azimah'

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الْعَرَبِيُّ مِنَ الْعَصْرِ الْأُمَوِيِّ مَدَحَ أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ فِي دِيوَانِهِ «الْهَاشِمِيَّاتِ»:
questions.question_english: The Umayyad poet who praised Ahl al-Bayt in his collection 'Al-Hashimiyyat' is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: صَاحِبُ دِيوَانِ الْهَاشِمِيَّاتِ فِي مَدْحِ أَهْلِ الْبَيْتِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of Diwan al-Hashimiyyat praising Ahl al-Bayt

questions.question_arabic: «الْمُعَذَّبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ» مِنْ تَأْلِيفِ :
questions.question_english: 'Al-Mu'adhdhabuna fi al-Ard' (The Sufferers on Earth) was authored by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَلِّفُ كِتَابِ «الْمُعَذَّبُونَ فِي الْأَرْضِ» طَهَ حُسَيْن
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Taha Hussein as author of The Sufferers on Earth

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الْأُمَوِيُّ الَّذِي قِيلَ فِيهِ: «إِنَّهُ يَغْرِفُ مِنْ بَحْرٍ»:
questions.question_english: The Umayyad poet of whom critics famously said: "He scoops from a vast ocean":
questions.explanation_arabic: قال النقاد في المقارنة بين فرسي رهان النقائض: الفرزدق ينحت من صخر لجزالة لغته، وجرير يغرف من بحر لسلاسة شعره وعذوبته.
questions.explanation_english: Classical critics noted that while al-Farazdaq carved from rock, Jarir scooped from an ocean of effortless natural verse.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَقُولَةُ يُونُسَ بْنِ حَبِيبٍ فِي أَنَّ جَرِيراً «يَغْرِفُ مِنْ بَحْرٍ» لِسُهُولَةِ شِعْرِهِ وَفَيْضِهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Critical maxim that Jarir 'scooped from an ocean' for his effortless lyrical flow

questions.question_arabic: الْأَدِيبُ الْمُعَاصِرُ لُقِّبَ بِـ «أَمِيرِ الْبَيَانِ» :
questions.question_english: The modern author given the title 'Prince of Eloquence' (Amir al-Bayan) is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ أَمِيرِ الْبَيَانِ لِلْأَمِيرِ شَكِيب أَرْسَلَان
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Title 'Amir al-Bayan' given to Shakib Arslan

questions.question_arabic: أُصِيبَ مُصْطَفَى صَادِق الرَّافِعِيُّ بِالصَّمَمِ وَهُوَ :
questions.question_english: Mustafa Sadiq al-Rafi'i was afflicted with deafness when he was:

options_arabic.A: صَغِيرُ السِّنِّ (فِي الثَّلَاثِينَ / فِي نَحْوِ الثَّلَاثِينَ)

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: إِصَابَةُ مُصْطَفَى صَادِق الرَّافِعِيِّ بِالصَّمَمِ فِي صِغَرِهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Mustafa Sadiq al-Rafi'i being afflicted with deafness

questions.question_arabic: وُلِدَ جَرِيرٌ فِي عَهْدِ خِلَافَةِ :
questions.question_english: The Umayyad poet Jarir was born during the Caliphate of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَوْلِدُ الشَّاعِرِ جَرِيرٍ فِي خِلَافَةِ عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Jarir's birth during the Caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan

questions.question_arabic: شَاعِرٌ امَوِيٌّ مِنْ بَنِي عُذْرَةَ تَغَنَّى بِمَعْشُوقَتِهِ، تُوُفِّيَ فِي مِصْرَ :
questions.question_english: An Umayyad poet of Banu Udhrah who sang of his beloved and passed away in Egypt:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَرْجَمَةُ شَاعِرِ الْغَزَلِ الْعُذْرِيِّ جَمِيلِ بْنِ مَعْمَرٍ (جَمِيلُ بُثَيْنَةَ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Biography of the Udhri ghazal poet Jamil ibn Ma'mar (Jamil Buthaynah)

questions.question_arabic: أَدِيبٌ وَنَاقِدٌ لُقِّبَ بِـ «عَمِيدِ الْأَدَبِ الْعَرَبِيِّ» :
questions.question_english: A writer and critic given the title 'Dean of Arabic Literature' (Amid al-Adab al-Arabi):
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ عَمِيدِ الْأَدَبِ الْعَرَبِيِّ لِلدُّكْتُورِ طَهَ حُسَيْن
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Title Dean of Arabic Literature given to Taha Hussein

questions.question_arabic: «جَاهِلِيَّةُ الْقَرْنِ الْعِشْرِينَ» مِنْ آثَارِ :
questions.question_english: 'Jahiliyyat al-Qarn al-Ishrin' (Twentieth Century Jahiliyyah) was authored by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَلِّفُ كِتَابِ «جَاهِلِيَّةِ الْقَرْنِ الْعِشْرِينَ» مُحَمَّد قُطْب
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Muhammad Qutb as author of Jahiliyyat al-Qarn al-Ishrin

questions.question_arabic: كَانَ الشَّاعِرُ الْأُمَوِيُّ جَافِيًا فِي طَبْعِهِ قَاسِيًا فِي تَعَامُلِهِ، جَرِيئًا فِي تَطَاوُلِهِ صَحْرَاوِيًّا فِي لُغَتِهِ، بَدَوِيًّا فِي مَعَانِيهِ، هُوَ:
questions.question_english: The Umayyad poet who was rough in temperament, harsh in dealings, bold in transgression, desert-like in his diction, and Bedouin in his meanings:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: خَصَائِصُ شَخْصِيَّةِ وَشِعْرِ الْفَرَزْدَقِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Temperament and Bedouin poetic style of al-Farazdaq

questions.question_arabic: قَصَرَ عُمَرُ بْنُ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ شِعْرَهُ عَلَى :
questions.question_english: Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah restricted his poetry to:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: اقْتِصَارُ شِعْرِ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ عَلَى الْغَزَلِ وَتَشْبِيبِ النِّسَاءِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah's focus on urban ghazal and women's descriptions

questions.question_arabic: رَائِدُ حُقُوقِ الْمَرْأَةِ فِي مِصْرَ (مُحَرِّرُ الْمَرْأَةِ) :
questions.question_english: The pioneer of women's liberation and rights in modern Egypt is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: رِيَادَةُ قَاسِم أَمِين فِي الدِّفَاعِ عَنْ حُقُوقِ الْمَرْأَةِ وَتَحْرِيرِهَا
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Qasim Amin's leadership in women's rights and reform

questions.question_arabic: مَنِ الْقَائِلُ عَنْ شِعْرِ جَرِيرٍ "إِنَّ جَرِيرًا يَغْرِفُ مِنْ بَحْرٍ" :
questions.question_english: Who said regarding Jarir's poetry: "Indeed Jarir scoops from an ocean":
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قَوْلُ الْأَخْطَلِ فِي الْمُوَازَنَةِ بَيْنَ جَرِيرٍ وَالْفَرَزْدَقِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Akhtal's critical remark comparing Jarir and al-Farazdaq

questions.question_arabic: مَا هِيَ الْقَبِيلَةُ الَّتِي يَنْتَمِي إِلَيْهَا الْأَخْطَلُ؟
questions.question_english: To which ancient Arab tribe did al-Akhtal belong?
questions.explanation_arabic: الأخطل هو غياث بن غوث بن الصلت التغلبي، شاعر قبيلة بني تغلب النصرانية ومفاخرها.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Akhtal (Ghiyath ibn Ghawth) was the supreme poet and spokesman of the Christian tribe of Banu Taghlib.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: انْتِمَاءُ الشَّاعِرِ الْأُمَوِيِّ الْأَخْطَلِ (غِيَاثِ بْنِ غَوْثٍ) إِلَى قَبِيلَةِ تَغْلِبَ النَّصْرَانِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Tribal affiliation of al-Akhtal with the Christian Arab tribe of Banu Taghlib

questions.question_arabic: كَانَ يَنْتَخِبُ شِعْرَهُ فَيَنْظِمُ تِسْعِينَ بَيْتًا وَيَخْتَارُ مِنْهَا ثَلَاثِينَ، هُوَ :
questions.question_english: He used to curate his poetry, composing ninety verses and selecting thirty among them; he is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: طَرِيقَةُ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ فِي انْتِخَابِ أَجْوَدِ شِعْرِهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah's method of refining and selecting his finest verses

questions.question_arabic: جَمِيلُ بُثَيْنَةَ شَاعِرُ الْعَصْرِ:
questions.question_english: Jamil Buthaynah was a poet of the:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: الْعَصْرُ الْأَدَبِيُّ لِجَمِيلِ بُثَيْنَةَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Literary era of Jamil Buthaynah

questions.question_arabic: أَسَّسَ جَامِعَةَ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ وَتَوَلَّى إِدَارَتَهَا:
questions.question_english: He founded Alexandria University (Farouk I University) and served as its rector:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَسِّسُ وَمُدِيرُ جَامِعَةِ الْإِسْكَنْدَرِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Founder and rector of Alexandria University

questions.question_arabic: هَجَا الْأَخْطَلُ فِي قَصَائِدِهِ (بِأَمْرِ يَزِيدَ بْنِ مُعَاوِيَةَ):
questions.question_english: Al-Akhtal satirized in his poems (at Yazid ibn Mu'awiyah's request):
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: هِجَاءُ الْأَخْطَلِ لِلْأَنْصَارِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Akhtal's political satire against the Ansar

questions.question_arabic: حَدِّدِ الزَّوْجَ الْخَطَأَ مِمَّا يَلِي:
questions.question_english: Identify the incorrect author-book pairing among the following:

B.english: Kahlil Gibran — The Earth Gods (Alihat al-Ard)

C.arabic: طَهَ حُسَيْن — مُسْتَقْبَلُ الثَّقَافَةِ فِي مِصْرَ
C.english: Taha Hussein — Mustaqbal al-Thaqafah fi Misr

D.english: Ahmad Amin — Khazanat al-Adab (by Abd al-Qadir al-Baghdadi)

questions.correct_answer_text_english: Ahmad Amin — Khazanat al-Adab (by Abd al-Qadir al-Baghdadi)
questions.explanation_arabic: موسوعة 'خزانة الأدب ولب لباب لسان العرب' ألفها عبد القادر البغدادي في شواهد شرح الكافية؛ وليس أحمد أمين.
questions.explanation_english: 'Khazanat al-Adab' is the famous classical philological encyclopedia compiled by Abd al-Qadir al-Baghdadi.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَصْحِيحُ نِسْبَةِ مَوْسُوعَةِ «خِزَانَةِ الْأَدَبِ» لِعَبْدِ الْقَادِرِ الْبَغْدَادِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Correcting attribution of 'Khazanat al-Adab' to Abd al-Qadir al-Baghdadi

questions.question_arabic: كَانَ جَمِيلُ بْنُ مَعْمَرٍ الْمُلَقَّبُ بِجَمِيلِ بُثَيْنَةَ يُحِبُّ ابْنَةَ عَمِّهِ فَشَكَا أَهْلُهَا إِلَى الْعَامِلِ فَهَرَبَ إِلَى الْيَمَنِ وَأَخِيرًا إِلَى مِصْرَ حَيْثُ :
questions.question_english: Jamil ibn Ma'mar loved his cousin, so her family complained to the governor; he fled to Yemen and finally to Egypt where:

options_arabic.C: مَرِضَ وَعَادَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ فِي وَادِي الْقُرَى وَعُولِجَ وَشُفِيَ
options_arabic.D: مَرِضَ وَعَادَ إِلَى أَهْلِهِ فِي وَادِي الْقُرَى وَتُوُفِّيَ

options_english.B: He fell ill, was treated, and recovered
options_english.C: He fell ill, returned to Wadi al-Qura, and recovered
options_english.D: He fell ill, returned, and died in Wadi al-Qura

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: وَفَاةُ جَمِيلِ بْنِ مَعْمَرٍ بِمِصْرَ إِثْرَ مَرَضِهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Jamil ibn Ma'mar falling ill and dying in Egypt

questions.question_arabic: «هَذَا الَّذِي تَعْرِفُ الْبَطْحَاءُ وَطْأَتَهُ ... وَالْبَيْتُ يَعْرِفُهُ وَالْحِلُّ وَالْحَرَمُ»، قَالَ الْفَرَزْدَقُ فِي مَدْحِ:
questions.question_english: "This is he whose footstep the valley of Mecca knows, and whom the Sacred House knows, the unhallowed land and the sanctuary." Al-Farazdaq said this in praise of:
questions.explanation_arabic: ارتجل الفرزدق هذه القصيدة الميمية العصماء في مكة المكرمة بحضرة هشام بن عبد الملك مدحاً لزين العابدين علي بن الحسين.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Farazdaq spontaneously declaimed this immortal ode before Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik in praise of Zayn al-Abidin.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ مِيمِيَّةِ الْفَرَزْدَقِ الْخَالِدَةِ فِي مَدْحِ عَلِيِّ بْنِ الْحُسَيْنِ زَيْنِ الْعَابِدِينَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of al-Farazdaq's masterwork ode to Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin

questions.question_arabic: شَاعِرٌ عَبَّاسِيٌّ اشْتُهِرَ فِي وَصْفِ الطَّبِيعَةِ وَتَشْخِيصِهَا:
questions.question_english: An Abbasid poet celebrated for his exquisite, vivid descriptions of nature:
questions.explanation_arabic: اشتهر ابن الرومي برسم لوحات بصرية دقيقة وبديعة في وصف الطبيعة والربيع والبساتين والرياض.
questions.explanation_english: Ibn al-Rumi was renowned for his rich sensory descriptions of natural scenery, flora, and seasonal beauty.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: بَرَاعَةُ ابْنِ الرُّومِيِّ فِي شِعْرِ وَصْفِ الطَّبِيعَةِ وَمَظَاهِرِ الْحَيَاةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Ibn al-Rumi's mastery in nature description and visual imagery

questions.question_arabic: وُلِدَ بِالْمَدِينَةِ لَيْلَةَ مَاتَ عُمَرُ وَقِيلَ فِيهِ أَيُّ حَقٍّ رُفِعَ وَأَيُّ بَاطِلٍ وُضِعَ :
questions.question_english: He was born in Medina on the night Caliph Umar died, and it was said of him: 'What truth was taken away, and what vanity was born!':
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَوْلِدُ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ وَالْقَوْلُ الْمَأْثُورُ فِيهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Birth of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah and the famous saying associated with it

questions.question_arabic:
رَتِّبِ الشُّعَرَاءَ الْمَذْكُورِينَ أَدْنَاهُ وَفْقاً لِتَوَارِيخِ وَفَيَاتِهِمْ مَعَ اسْتِخْدَامِ الشِّفْرَةِ التَّالِيَةِ: (اقْرَأ الشِّفْرَةَ مِنَ الْيَمِينِ)
(a) الْأَعْشَى مَيْمُون بْن قَيْس (ت نَحْوَ 7 هـ / 629 م)
(b) عُمَرُ بْنُ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ (ت نَحْوَ 93 هـ / 712 م)
(c) حَاتِمٌ الطَّائِيُّ (ت نَحْوَ 605 م — قَبْلَ الْهِجْرَةِ)
(d) عَمْرُو بْنُ مَعْدِيكَرِبَ الزُّبَيْدِيُّ (ت 21 هـ / 642 م)
questions.question_english:
Arrange the following classical poets in chronological order of their deaths (Read code from the right):
(a) Al-A'sha (~629 CE / 7 AH)
(b) Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah (~712 CE / 93 AH)
(c) Hatim al-Ta'i (~605 CE)
(d) Amr ibn Ma'dikarib (~642 CE / 21 AH)

C.english: (b) Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah -> (d) Amr ibn Ma'dikarib -> (a) Al-A'sha -> (c) Hatim al-Ta'i (from right)

questions.correct_answer_text_english: (b) Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah -> (d) Amr ibn Ma'dikarib -> (a) Al-A'sha -> (c) Hatim al-Ta'i (from right)
questions.explanation_arabic: تسلسل الوفيات: حاتم الطائي في الجاهلية (c) -> الأعشى في أوائل الهجرة (a) -> عمرو بن معديكرب في معركة القادسية/نهاوند (d) -> عمر بن أبي ربيعة في العصر الأموي (b).
questions.explanation_english: Chronology of death: Hatim al-Ta'i (c. 605 CE), Al-A'sha (c. 629 CE), Amr ibn Ma'dikarib (c. 642 CE), Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah (c. 712 CE).
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: التَّرْتِيبُ التَّارِيخِيُّ لِوَفَيَاتِ الشُّعَرَاءِ: حَاتِمٌ الطَّائِيُّ ثُمَّ الْأَعْشَى ثُمَّ عَمْرُو بْنُ مَعْدِيكَرِبَ ثُمَّ عُمَرُ بْنُ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Death chronology: Hatim al-Ta'i (c. 605), Al-A'sha (c. 629), Amr ibn Ma'dikarib (c. 642), Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah (c. 712)

questions.question_arabic: مُصْطَفَى صَادِقٌ الرَّافِعِيُّ فِي كِتَابِهِ «أَوْرَاقُ الْوَرْدِ» يَبْحَثُ آرَاءَهُ فِي:
questions.question_english: Mustafa Sadiq al-Rafi'i, in his book 'Awraq al-Ward', discusses his views on:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَوْضُوعُ كِتَابِ أَوْرَاقِ الْوَرْدِ لِلرَّافِعِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Subject matter of al-Rafi'i's book Awraq al-Ward

questions.question_arabic: شَاعِرٌ جَاهِلِيٌّ مِنْ رُؤَسَاءِ ثَقِيفٍ نَبَذَ الْأَصْنَامَ وَدَعَا إِلَى التَّوْحِيدِ (مِنَ الْحُنَفَاءِ):
questions.question_english: A pre-Islamic poet and leader of Thaqif who rejected idols and called for monotheism (among the Hunafa):
questions.explanation_arabic: أمية بن أبي الصلت الثقفي شاعر جاهلي حكيم من الحنفاء الذين قرأوا الكتب القديمة وتحدثوا عن التوحيد والبعث.
questions.explanation_english: Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt of Taif was a prominent pre-Islamic monotheist (Hanif) poet.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَرْجَمَةُ أُمَيَّةَ بْنِ أَبِي الصَّلْتِ الثَّقَفِيِّ وَدَعْوَتُهُ التَّوْحِيدِيَّةُ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Biography of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt and his monotheistic poetry

questions.question_arabic: وُلِدَ عَبَّاس مَحْمُود الْعَقَّاد فِي مَدِينَةِ:
questions.question_english: Abbas Mahmud al-Aqqad was born in the city of:
questions.explanation_arabic: ولد عملاق الفكر العربي عباس محمود العقاد في مدينة أسوان بصعيد مصر عام 1889 م وعاش مكافحاً حتى أصبح عَلماً بارزاً.
questions.explanation_english: Abbas Mahmud al-Aqqad was born in Aswan in Upper Egypt in 1889, rising through self-education to become a titan of Arabic letters.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَسْقِطُ رَأْسِ الْعَلَّامَةِ عَبَّاس مَحْمُود الْعَقَّاد فِي مَدِينَةِ أَسْوَانَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Birthplace of Abbas Mahmud al-Aqqad in Aswan

questions.question_arabic: تَنْتَمِي اللُّغَةُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ إِلَى فَصِيلَةِ:
questions.question_english: The Arabic language belongs to the family of:
questions.explanation_arabic: تنتمي اللغة العربية إلى فرع اللغات السامية الوسطى والجنوبية ضمن عائلة اللغات الأفروآسيوية.
questions.explanation_english: Arabic is a major Central Semitic language within the Afroasiatic language phylum.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَصْنِيفُ اللُّغَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ ضِمْنَ أُسْرَةِ اللُّغَاتِ السَّامِيَّةِ الْجَنُوبِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Classifying Arabic within the Semitic language family

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ كِبَارِ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْجَاهِلِيِّينَ:
questions.question_english: Among the great Pre-Islamic (Jahili) poets:
questions.explanation_arabic: ميمون بن قيس (الأعشى) من كبار شعراء الطبقة الأولى في الجاهلية وصاحب المعلقة الدالية: ودع هريرة إن الركب مرتحل.
questions.explanation_english: Al-A'sha Maymun ibn Qays is a towering pre-Islamic poet and author of the famous Daliyyah Mu'allaqah.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَصْنِيفُ أَعْشَى قَيْسٍ ضِمْنَ فُحُولِ شُعَرَاءِ الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Classifying A'sha Qays among the major pre-Islamic master poets

questions.question_arabic: يُرْجِعُ الْمُؤَرِّخُونَ الْعَرَبَ إِلَى ثَلَاثِ طَبَقَاتٍ وَهِيَ :
questions.question_english: Historians classify the Arabs into three main divisions, which are:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: طَبَقَاتُ الْعَرَبِ الثَّلَاثُ عِنْدَ الْمُؤَرِّخِينَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The three divisions of the Arabs according to historians

questions.question_arabic: يَرُدُّ الْعُلَمَاءُ اللُّغَاتِ السَّامِيَّةَ إِلَى :
questions.question_english: Scholars trace the Semitic language family to:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَهَمُّ فُرُوعِ وَتَقْسِيمَاتِ اللُّغَاتِ السَّامِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Main branches and divisions of the Semitic language family

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ تَأْلِيفِ أَحْمَدَ حَسَنِ الزَّيَّاتِ :
questions.question_english: Among the celebrated works of Ahmad Hasan al-Zayyat is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: كِتَابُ تَارِيخِ الْأَدَبِ الْعَرَبِيِّ لِأَحْمَدَ حَسَن الزَّيَّاتِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Tarikh al-Adab al-Arabi by Ahmad Hasan al-Zayyat

questions.question_arabic: "مَا انْتَهَى الَيْكُمْ مِمَّا قَالَتِ الْعَرَبُ الَّا أَقَلُّهُ" قَالَهُ :
questions.question_english: "Nothing has reached you of what the Arabs said except the least of it." This was said by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قَائِلُ عِبَارَةِ: مَا انْتَهَى إِلَيْكُمْ مِمَّا قَالَتِ الْعَرَبُ إِلَّا أَقَلُّهُ (أَبُو عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَلَاءِ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Speaker of the famous statement on the transmission of Pre-Islamic Arabic poetry (Abu Amr ibn al-Ala)

questions.question_arabic: لُغَةُ الْيَمَنِ هِيَ أَكْثَرُ اتِّصَالاً بِاللُّغَةِ:
questions.question_english: The ancient language of Yemen (South Semitic) is most closely connected to:
questions.explanation_arabic: اللغة الحميرية والسبئية في اليمن تنتمي للفرع السامي الجنوبي وهي شديدة القرب من الحبشية (الجعزية).
questions.explanation_english: Ancient South Arabian (Himyaritic/Sabaic) and Ethiopic (Ge'ez) belong to the South Semitic language branch.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: عَلَاقَةُ لُغَةِ الْيَمَنِ الْحِمْيَرِيَّةِ بِاللُّغَةِ الْحَبَشِيَّةِ ضِمْنَ السَّامِيَّةِ الْجَنُوبِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Relationship of South Arabian (Yemeni) languages to Ethiopic within South Semitic

questions.question_arabic: قَدْ وَرِثَ خَلِيل مُطْرَان الْقَرِيحَةَ وَالْمَوْهِبَةَ الشِّعْرِيَّةَ عَنْ:
questions.question_english: Khalil Mutran inherited his poetic talent and sensitivity from:
questions.explanation_arabic: كانت والدة خليل مطران السيدة ملكة الصباغ شاعرة وأديبة ذات ذوق رفيع غرست في نفسه حب الشعر والبيان.
questions.explanation_english: Khalil Mutran inherited his poetic sensitivity from his cultured mother, Malakah al-Sabbagh, who composed poetry.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَأَثُّرُ خَلِيل مُطْرَان بِمَوْهِبَةِ وَالِدَتِهِ مَلَكَة الصَّبَّاغ الشِّعْرِيَّةِ وَالْأَدَبِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Khalil Mutran's inheritance of poetic aptitude from his mother Malakah al-Sabbagh

questions.question_arabic: إِذَا الْمَرْءُ لَمْ يَدْنَسْ مِنَ اللُّؤْمِ عِرْضُهُ فَكُلُّ رِدَاءٍ يَرْتَدِيهِ جَمِيلُ قَالَهُ :
questions.question_english: "If a man's honor is not soiled by baseness, then every garment he wears is beautiful." Said by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قَائِلُ بَيْتِ: إِذَا الْمَرْءُ لَمْ يَدْنَسْ مِنَ اللُّؤْمِ عِرْضُهُ (السَّمَوْأَلُ بْنُ عَادِيَاءَ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of the verse: 'If a man's honor is not soiled by baseness' (Al-Samaw'al ibn Adiya)

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ الدُّكْتُورِ شَوْقِي ضَيْف:
questions.question_english: Which of the following is not among the works authored by Dr. Shawqi Dayf:
questions.explanation_arabic: ألف شوقي ضيف 'المدارس النحوية' و'في النقد الأدبي' و'البارودي' وسلسلة تاريخ الأدب العربي؛ أما 'الفصول' فهو للعقاد.
questions.explanation_english: Dr. Shawqi Dayf authored 'Al-Madaris al-Nahwiyyah' and 'Fi al-Naqd al-Adabi', whereas 'Al-Fusul' is by Abbas Mahmud al-Aqqad.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ كُتُبِ د. شَوْقِي ضَيْف عَنْ كِتَابِ «الْفُصُولِ» لِعَبَّاس مَحْمُود الْعَقَّاد
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing Dr. Shawqi Dayf's scholarship from al-Aqqad's 'Al-Fusul'

questions.question_arabic: أَوَّلُ مَدِينَةٍ أَسَّسَهَا الْعَرَبُ فِي مِصْرَ:
questions.question_english: The first city founded by the Arabs in Egypt:
questions.explanation_arabic: أسس القائد عمرو بن العاص مدينة الفسطاط عام 20 هـ (641 م) وبنى فيها جامعه الشهير كأول عاصمة إسلامية لمصر.
questions.explanation_english: Amr ibn al-Aas founded al-Fustat in 641 CE as the first Arab/Islamic city in Egypt.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ مَدِينَةِ الْفُسْطَاطِ كَأَوَّلِ مَدِينَةٍ إِسْلَامِيَّةٍ أَسَّسَهَا عَمْرُو بْنُ الْعَاصِ فِي مِصْرَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying al-Fustat as the first city founded by Amr ibn al-Aas in Egypt

questions.question_arabic:
اقْرَأِ الْأَشْعَارَ التَّالِيَةَ وَأَجِبْ عَنِ الْأَسْئِلَةِ فِيمَا يَلِي :
«تَرَى بَعَرَ الْآرَامِ فِي عَرَصَاتِهَا *** وَقِيعَانِهَا كَأَنَّهُ حَبُّ فُلْفُلِ»
«إِذَا قَامَتَا تَضَوَّعَ الْمِسْكُ مِنْهُمَا *** نَسِيمَ الصَّبَا جَاءَتْ بِرَيَّا الْقَرَنْفُلِ»
مَنْ قَالَ هَذِهِ الْأَشْعَارَ :
questions.question_english: Read the following verses and answer the questions that follow: 'You see the dung of white antelopes in its courtyards and depressions as though it were peppercorns...' Who is the poet of these verses?
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ أَبْيَاتِ وَصْفِ الدِّيَارِ لِامْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ فِي مُعَلَّقَتِهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the ruined-abode verses to Imru' al-Qais

questions.question_arabic: «إِذَا بَلَغَ الْفِطَامَ لَنَا صَبِيٌّ ... تَخِرُّ لَهُ الْجَبَابِرُ سَاجِدِينَا»، قَالَهُ:
questions.question_english: "When a child of ours reaches weaning age, tyrants bow down before him in submission." The author of this verse is:
questions.explanation_arabic: البيت من معلقة عمرو بن كلثوم التغلبي الشهيرة التي تعد من مفاخر العرب في الجاهلية.
questions.explanation_english: This famous verse is from the Mu'allaqah of Amr ibn Kulthum al-Taghlibi.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتٍ مِنْ مُعَلَّقَةِ عَمْرِو بْنِ كُلْثُومٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of a famous verse from the Mu'allaqah of Amr ibn Kulthum

questions.question_arabic: أَبُو فِرَاسٍ هَمَّامُ بْنُ غَالِبٍ هُوَ شَاعِرٌ أُمَوِيٌّ مُلَقَّبٌ بِـ:
questions.question_english: Abu Firas Hammam ibn Ghalib is an Umayyad poet nicknamed:
questions.explanation_arabic: الفرزدق لقبه همام بن غالب بن صعصعة الدارمي التميمي، وسمي الفرزدق لغلظ وجهه وقصر قامته تشبيهاً برغيف الخبز الضخم.
questions.explanation_english: Hammam ibn Ghalib al-Tamimi was nicknamed 'Al-Farazdaq' (lump of dough) due to his stocky build and rugged facial features.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ لَقَبِ «الْفَرَزْدَقِ» لِلشَّاعِرِ هَمَّامِ بْنِ غَالِبٍ التَّمِيمِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the nickname 'Al-Farazdaq' for Hammam ibn Ghalib al-Tamimi

questions.question_arabic: تَخَرَّجَ الْكَاتِبُ وَالرِّوَائِيُّ إِحْسَان عَبْد الْقُدُّوس فِي كُلِّيَّةِ:
questions.question_english: The novelist Ihsan Abdel Quddous graduated from the Faculty of:
questions.explanation_arabic: تخرج إحسان عبد القدوس في كلية الحقوق بجامعة القاهرة عام 1942 م وعمل بالمحاماة فترة قصيرة قبل تفرغه للصحافة والأدب.
questions.explanation_english: Ihsan Abdel Quddous graduated from the Faculty of Law at Cairo University in 1942 before devoting himself to journalism and fiction.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: دِرَاسَةُ إِحْسَان عَبْد الْقُدُّوس الْجَامِعِيَّةُ فِي كُلِّيَّةِ الْحُقُوقِ بِجَامِعَةِ الْقَاهِرَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: University education of Ihsan Abdel Quddous at Cairo University Faculty of Law

questions.question_arabic: قَدْ ضَاعَ الْكَثِيرُ مِنْ شِعْرِ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ وَبَقِيَ دِيوَانٌ صَغِيرٌ يَحْوِي نَحْواً مِنْ:
questions.question_english: Much of Imru' al-Qais's poetry was lost, and only a slender diwan survived containing approximately:
questions.explanation_arabic: يضم ديوان امرئ القيس برواية الأصمعي والسكري نحواً من 25 قصيدة ومقطوعة مشهورة.
questions.explanation_english: The extant Diwan of Imru' al-Qais according to classical recensions comprises around 25 authentic poems and fragments.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: عَدَدُ الْقَصَائِدِ وَالْمَقْطُوعَاتِ فِي دِيوَانِ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ الْمَحْفُوظِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Approximate number of preserved poems in the Diwan of Imru' al-Qais

questions.question_arabic: كَانَ يَلْقَى كَثِيراً مِنَ الْإِهْمَالِ فِي أَوَّلِ أَمْرِهِ حَتَّى كَانَ يُضْطَرُّ أَنْ يَنْسُبَ أَعْمَالَهُ إِلَى بَعْضِ الْقُدَمَاءِ لِتَنَالَ الْقَبُولَ:
questions.question_english: He initially faced neglect and rejection, to the extent that he was compelled to attribute his early writings to ancient scholars for them to be accepted:
questions.explanation_arabic: ذكر الجاحظ بنفسه أنه كان يؤلف الرسائل البليغة فينسبها لابن المقفع أو سهل بن هارون فيقبل الناس عليها ويتداولونها لجودة نصها.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Jahiz famously recounted that in his youth he would pseudonymously attribute his writings to famous masters like Ibn al-Muqaffa so that audiences would read them.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: حِيلَةُ الْجَاحِظِ فِي نِسْبَةِ كُتُبِهِ فِي صِبَاهُ إِلَى ابْنِ الْمُقَفَّعِ أَوْ سَهْلِ بْنِ هَارُونَ لِرَوَاجِهَا
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Jahiz's tactic of attributing his early books to Ibn al-Muqaffa to gain readership

questions.question_arabic: عُلَمَاءُ الْغَرْبِ لَدَيْهِمْ مَعْرِفَةٌ أَدَقُّ عَنْ:
questions.question_english: According to the passage, Western scholars have more meticulous knowledge regarding:
questions.context_paragraph_arabic: «وَوَجَدْتُ فِي الْغَزَالِيِّ مَا يَجْعَلُهُ حَلْقَةً ذَهَبِيَّةً مُوَصِّلَةً بَيْنَ الَّذِينَ تَقَدَّمُوهُ مِنْ مُتَصَوِّفِي الْهِنْدِ وَالَّذِينَ جَاؤُوا بَعْدَهُ مِنَ الْإِلَهِيِّينَ. فَفِي مَا بَلَغَتْ إِلَيْهِ أَفْكَارُ الْبُوذِيِّينَ قَدِيمًا شَيْءٌ مِنْ مُيُولِ الْغَزَالِيِّ، وَفِي مَا كَتَبَهُ سِبِينُوزَا وَوِلْيَم بْلَايْك حَدِيثًا شَيْءٌ مِنْ عَوَاطِفِهِ. وَلِلْغَزَالِيِّ عِنْدَ مُسْتَشْرِقِي الْغَرْبِ وَعُلَمَائِهِ مَنْزِلَةٌ رَفِيعَةٌ، وَهُمْ يَضَعُونَهُ مَعَ ابْنِ سِينَا وَابْنِ رُشْدٍ فِي الْمَقَامِ الْأَوَّلِ بَيْنَ فَلَاسِفَةِ الشَّرْقِ، أَمَّا الرُّوحِيُّونَ بَيْنَهُمْ فَيَحْسَبُونَهُ أَنْبَلَ وَأَسْمَى فِكْرَةٍ ظَهَرَتْ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ، وَمِنَ الْغَرَائِبِ أَنَّنِي شَاهَدْتُ عَلَى جُدْرَانِ كَنِيسَةٍ فِي فِلُورَنْسَا (إِيطَالْيَا) مِنْ بِنَاءِ الْجِيلِ الْخَامِسَ عَشَرَ صُورَةَ الْغَزَالِيِّ بَيْنَ صُوَرِ غَيْرِهِ مِنَ الْفَلَاسِفَةِ وَالْقِدِّيسِينَ وَاللَّاهُوتِيِّينَ الَّذِينَ تَعْتَبِرُهُمْ أَئِمَّةُ الْكَنِيسَةِ فِي الْأَجْيَالِ الْوُسْطَى دَعَائِمَ وَأَعْمِدَةً فِي هَيْكَلِ الرُّوحِ الْمُطْلَقِ. وَلَكِنَّ الْأَغْرَبَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ هُوَ أَنَّ الْغَرْبِيِّينَ يَعْرِفُونَ عَنِ الْغَزَالِيِّ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا يَعْرِفُهُ الشَّرْقِيُّونَ. فَهُمْ يُتَرْجِمُونَهُ وَيَبْحَثُونَ فِي تَعَالِيمِهِ وَيُدَقِّقُونَ النَّظَرَ فِي مَنَازِعِهِ الْفَلْسَفِيَّةِ وَمَرَامِيهِ الصُّوفِيَّةِ. أَمَّا نَحْنُ، نَحْنُ الَّذِينَ لَمْ نَزَلْ نَتَكَلَّمُ اللُّغَةَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَنَكْتُبُهَا، فَقَلَّمَا ذَكَرْنَا الْغَزَالِيَّ أَوْ تَحَدَّثْنَا عَنْهُ. نَحْنُ لَمْ نَزَلْ مَشْغُولِينَ بِالْأَصْدَافِ كَأَنَّ الْأَصْدَافَ هِيَ كُلُّ مَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَحْرِ الْحَيَاةِ إِلَى شَوَاطِئِ الْأَيَّامِ وَاللَّيَالِي.»
questions.context_paragraph_english: "I found in Al-Ghazali what makes him a golden connecting link between the Indian mystics who preceded him and the theists who came after him. In ancient Buddhist thought there is something of Al-Ghazali's inclinations, and in the modern writings of Spinoza and William Blake there is something of his sentiments. Western orientalists and scholars hold Al-Ghazali in high esteem, placing him alongside Avicenna and Averroes in the foremost rank among Eastern philosophers. Spiritual thinkers among them regard him as the noblest and loftiest intellect in Islam. Remarkably, on the walls of a 15th-century church in Florence, Italy, I witnessed Al-Ghazali's image among the portraits of philosophers, saints, and theologians whom church authorities in the Middle Ages considered pillars of absolute spirituality. Yet stranger still, Westerners know more about Al-Ghazali than Easterners do; they translate him, study his teachings, and examine his philosophical and mystical goals closely, whereas we who still speak and write Arabic rarely mention or discuss him..."

options_english.C: Philosophy and mystical teachings of Al-Ghazali

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: عِنَايَةُ عُلَمَاءِ الْغَرْبِ بِفَلْسَفَةِ وَتَعَالِيمِ الْغَزَالِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Western scholarly focus on the philosophy and mystical teachings of Al-Ghazali

questions.question_arabic: «إِنِّي أَرَى فِيكَ مَخَايِلَ أَرَى أَنْ لَا تُضَيِّعَهَا وَسَتَقُولُ الشِّعْرَ فَاصْحَبْنِي أُخَرِّجْكَ»، قَالَهُ وَالِبَةُ بْنُ الْحُبَابِ فِي :
questions.question_english: 'Indeed I see in you marks of brilliance that I wish you not to waste; you will surely compose poetry, so accompany me and I shall train you.' Walibah ibn al-Hubab said this regarding:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَتَلْمُذُ أَبِي نُوَاسٍ عَلَى يَدِ وَالِبَةَ بْنِ الْحُبَابِ الْكُوفِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Abu Nuwas's mentorship under Walibah ibn al-Hubab

questions.question_arabic: أَكْثَرُ شِعْرِ حَسَّانَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ فِي:
questions.question_english: The majority of Hassan ibn Thabit's poetry after Islam was dedicated to:
questions.explanation_arabic: كرس حسان بن ثابت موهبته في صدر الإسلام لمهاجاة شعراء قريش والرد على تطاولهم والدفاع عن النبي ﷺ.
questions.explanation_english: Hassan ibn Thabit dedicated the bulk of his poetic output in the Islamic era to satirical polemics against the polytheists.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: غَلَبَةُ الْهِجَاءِ وَالدِّفَاعِ عَنِ الدَّعْوَةِ عَلَى شِعْرِ حَسَّانَ فِي الْإِسْلَامِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Predominance of satire against pagans and ideological defense in Hassan's Islamic poetry

questions.question_arabic: «النَّظَرَاتُ» لِلْمَنْفَلُوطِيِّ هِيَ مَجْمُوعَةٌ مِنَ الْمَقَالَاتِ:
questions.question_english: "Al-Nazarat" by al-Manfaluti is primarily a collection of essays that are:
questions.explanation_arabic: تتميز مقالات النظرات للمنفلوطي بطابعها الاجتماعي والأخلاقي والإنساني الذي دعا فيه إلى إصلاح المجتمع والرحمة بالضعفاء.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Manfaluti's 'Al-Nazarat' is famous for its eloquent social, ethical, and reformist essays championing the poor.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: الطَّابَعُ الِاجْتِمَاعِيُّ وَالْإِصْلَاحِيُّ لِمَقَالَاتِ «النَّظَرَاتِ» لِلْمَنْفَلُوطِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Social, moral, and reformist character of al-Manfaluti's 'Al-Nazarat'

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الْأُمَوِيُّ الَّذِي كَانَ أَبُوهُ عَامِلًا عَلَى وِلَايَةِ الْجَنَدِ فِي الْيَمَنِ مِنْ قِبَلِ النَّبِيِّ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ ثُمَّ مِنْ قِبَلِ الْخُلَفَاءِ الرَّاشِدِينَ:
questions.question_english: The Umayyad poet whose father was governor over the province of al-Janad in Yemen on behalf of the Prophet Muhammad, and then under the Rightly-Guided Caliphs:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: سِيرَةُ وَالِدِ الشَّاعِرِ عُمَرَ بْنِ أَبِي رَبِيعَةَ وَعَمَلُهُ فِي الْيَمَنِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Governorship of Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah's father over al-Janad in Yemen

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الْجَاهِلِيُّ قُتِلَ وَهُوَ دُونَ ثَلَاثِينَ:
questions.question_english: The Pre-Islamic poet who was killed before reaching the age of thirty is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَقْتَلُ الشَّاعِرِ طَرَفَةَ بْنِ الْعَبْدِ شَابّاً
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The killing of Tarafah ibn al-Abd at a young age

questions.question_arabic:
هَذَا الشِّعْرُ مِنْ مُعَلَّقَةِ:
يَا دَارَ مَيَّةَ بِالْعَلْيَاءِ فَالسَّنَدِ ... أَقْوَتْ وَطَالَ عَلَيْهَا سَالِفُ الْأَبَدِ
questions.question_english:
This verse belongs to the Mu'allaqah of:
'O abode of Mayyah on the high ground and the slope, desolate and worn by the long past ages':
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَطْلَعُ مُعَلَّقَةِ النَّابِغَةِ الذُّبْيَانِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Opening of the Mu'allaqah of al-Nabighah al-Dhubyani

questions.question_arabic: حَاوَلَ امْرُؤُ الْقَيْسِ أَنْ يَسْتَرْجِعَ مَمْلَكَةَ أَبِيهِ مِنْ مُلُوكِ:
questions.question_english: Imru' al-Qais attempted to reclaim his father's kingdom from the kings of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُحَاوَلَةُ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ اسْتِرْجَاعَ مُلْكِ أَبِيهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Imru' al-Qais's attempt to reclaim his father's realm

questions.question_arabic: مَا أَرَانَا نَقُولُ إِلَّا مُعَارًا أَوْ مُعَادًا مِنْ قَوْلِنَا مَكْرُورًا : قَالَهُ
questions.question_english: "I see that we say nothing except what is borrowed, or repeated from our speech over again." This was said by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قَائِلُ بَيْتِ: مَا أَرَانَا نَقُولُ إِلَّا مُعَارًا
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of the verse: 'I see that we say nothing except what is borrowed'

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الْجَاهِلِيُّ الْأَوْحَدُ الَّذِي نُصِبَتْ لَهُ خَيْمَةٌ (مِنْ أَدَمٍ حَمْرَاءَ) فِي سُوقِ عُكَاظٍ:
questions.question_english: The preeminent Pre-Islamic poet for whom a red leather pavilion was pitched at Suq Ukaz to judge poetry:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قُبَّةُ النَّابِغَةِ الذُّبْيَانِيِّ لِلتَّحْكِيمِ فِي عُكَاظٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Nabighah's pavilion for judging poetry at Ukaz

questions.question_arabic: عَاصِمَةُ الْعِرَاقِ :
questions.question_english: The capital of Iraq is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: عَاصِمَةُ جُمْهُورِيَّةِ الْعِرَاقِ (بَغْدَادُ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Capital of Iraq (Baghdad)

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ أَهَمِّ رُوَّادِ حَرَكَةِ الشِّعْرِ الْحُرِّ (شِعْرِ التَّفْعِيلَةِ) فِي مِصْرَ:
questions.question_english: Among the foremost pioneers of the Arabic Free Verse (Taf'ilah) movement in Egypt:
questions.explanation_arabic: صلاح عبد الصبور وأحمد عبد المعطي حجازي هما رائدا حركة شعر التفعيلة في مصر منذ أواخر الخمسينيات.
questions.explanation_english: Salah Abd al-Sabur is universally recognized as the pioneering leader of Free Verse poetry in Egypt.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: رِيَادَةُ صَلَاح عَبْد الصَّبُور لِحَرَكَةِ شِعْرِ التَّفْعِيلَةِ فِي مِصْرَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Salah Abd al-Sabur's pioneering leadership of the Free Verse movement in Egypt

questions.question_arabic: أَكْبَرُ دَوْلَةٍ عَرَبِيَّةٍ مِنْ حَيْثُ عَدَدُ السُّكَّانِ :
questions.question_english: The largest Arab country in terms of population size is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَكْبَرُ دَوْلَةٍ عَرَبِيَّةٍ سُكَّاناً (مِصْرُ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Most populous Arab country (Egypt)

questions.question_arabic:
«هَلْ غَادَرَ الشُّعَرَاءُ مِنْ مُتَرَدَّمِ
أَمْ هَلْ عَرَفْتَ الدَّارَ بَعْدَ تَوَهُّمِ»
مَعْنَى الْبَيْتِ:
questions.question_english: "Have the poets left any theme unstitched? Or did you recognize the abode after long uncertainty?" The meaning of the verse is:

options_arabic.A: لَمْ يَتْرُكِ الشُّعَرَاءُ مِنَ الْمَعَانِي إِلَّا وَقَدْ تَنَاوَلُوهَا
options_arabic.B: لَقَدْ غَادَرَ الشُّعَرَاءُ وَتَنَقَّلُوا مِنْ مَكَانِ الْمُتَرَدَّمِ

options_english.A: The poets left no meaning without having already addressed it
options_english.B: The poets departed and traveled from the place
options_english.C: The poets did not leave their dwelling places
options_english.D: The poets did not treat many poetic themes

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْنَى مَطْلَعِ مُعَلَّقَةِ عَنْتَرَةَ «هَلْ غَادَرَ الشُّعَرَاءُ مِنْ مُتَرَدَّمِ»
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Meaning of the opening verse of Antarah's Mu'allaqah

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ قَائِلُ: «قِفَا نَبْكِ مِنْ ذِكْرَى حَبِيبٍ وَمَنْزِلِ / بِسِقْطِ اللِّوَى بَيْنَ الدَّخُولِ فَحَوْمَلِ»:
questions.question_english: Who is the poet of: 'Halt, let us weep at the remembrance of a beloved and an abode, at the dune's edge between Al-Dakhul and Hawmal'?
questions.explanation_arabic: هذا هو مطلع معلقة امرئ القيس الكندي اللامية الشهيرة وهو أول من استوقف وبكى واستبكى على الديار.
questions.explanation_english: This is the iconic opening line of Imru' al-Qais's Mu'allaqah, inaugurating the classical tradition of weeping at the ruins.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ مَطْلَعِ أَشْهَرِ الْمُعَلَّقَاتِ إِلَى امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attributing the opening of the most famous Mu'allaqah to Imru' al-Qais

questions.question_arabic: شَاعِرٌ كَبِيرٌ قِيلَ إِنَّهُ أَوَّلُ مَنْ وَقَفَ عَلَى الْأَطْلَالِ وَبَكَى عَلَى الدِّيَارِ وَشَبَّبَ بِالنِّسَاءِ:
questions.question_english: A great poet said to be the first to halt at the ruins, weep over deserted abodes, and describe women with fine lyrics:
questions.explanation_arabic: أجمع رواة ونقاد الشعر العربي على أن امرأ القيس هو أول من قيد الأوابد واستوقف وبكى في مستهل القصائد.
questions.explanation_english: Early critics agreed that Imru' al-Qais pioneered the tradition of the nasib (halting and weeping at deserted campsites).
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: رِيَادَةُ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ فِي الْوُقُوفِ عَلَى الْأَطْلَالِ وَاسْتِيقَافِ الرَّكْبِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Imru' al-Qais's innovation of halting at ruins and weeping over lost abodes

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ قَائِلُ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: «فَإِنْ كُنْتَ لَا تَسْتَطِيعُ دَفْعَ مَنِيَّتِي / فَدَعْنِي أُبَادِرْهَا بِمَا مَلَكَتْ يَدِي»:
questions.question_english: Who is the poet of: 'If you cannot ward off my appointed death, then leave me to hasten towards it with whatever my hand possesses'?
questions.explanation_arabic: هذا البيت من عيون أبيات معلقة طرفة بن العبد البكري التي مطلعها: لخولة أطلال ببرقة ثهمد.
questions.explanation_english: This famous verse is from the Mu'allaqah of Tarafah ibn al-Abd al-Bakri expressing his existential hedonism.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ الْفَلْسَفَةِ وَالْإِقْبَالِ عَلَى الْحَيَاةِ إِلَى مُعَلَّقَةِ طَرَفَةَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attributing the existential verse on seizing life to Tarafah's Mu'allaqah

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ أَرْكَانِ النَّهْضَةِ الْعِلْمِيَّةِ الْحَدِيثَةِ فِي مِصْرَ لَهُ مُؤَلَّفَاتٌ مِنْهَا فِي تَارِيخِ مِصْرَ وَ تَخْلِيصُ الابْرِيزِ :
questions.question_english: One of the pillars of modern intellectual and scientific revival in Egypt; among his works are history of Egypt and Takhlis al-Ibriz:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مُؤَلِّفُ تَخْلِيصِ الْإِبْرِيزِ فِي تَلْخِيصِ بَارِيز وَرَائِدُ النَّهْضَةِ (رِفَاعَةُ الطَّهْطَاوِيُّ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of Takhlis al-Ibriz fi Talkhis Bariz and Nahda pioneer (Rifa'ah al-Tahtawi)

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ مُؤَلَّفَاتِ خَلِيل مُطْرَان:
questions.question_english: Which of the following is not a work authored by Khalil Mutran:
questions.explanation_arabic: 'ديوان الخليل' بأجزائه الأربعة وقصيدة 'الأسد الباكي' و'آثار بعلبك' من روائع مطران؛ أما 'حكايات بعلبك' فليس من كتبه.
questions.explanation_english: 'Diwan al-Khalil', 'Al-Asad al-Baki', and 'Athar Baalbek' are celebrated poems and collections by Mutran.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ قَصَائِدِ وَمُؤَلَّفَاتِ خَلِيل مُطْرَان عَنْ عُنْوَانِ «حِكَايَاتِ بَعْلَبَكَّ»
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing Khalil Mutran's works from 'Hikayat Baalbek'

questions.question_arabic: «مَا أَرَانَا نَقُولُ إِلَّا مُعَاراً / وَمُعَاداً مِنْ قَوْلِنَا مَكْرُوراً»، قَالَهُ:
questions.question_english: Who is the poet of: 'I see that we only say what has been borrowed, and repeated over again from our words'?
questions.explanation_arabic: هذا البيت لزهير بن أبي سلمى يعبر فيه عن شعوره بأن المعاني الشعرية استنفدها الأوائل وصار المتأخرون يعيدونها.
questions.explanation_english: Composed by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma reflecting on how classical poetic themes are inherited and re-fashioned.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ تَنَاوُلِ الْمَعَانِي الشِّعْرِيَّةِ إِلَى زُهَيْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلْمَى
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attributing the verse on poetic imitation and inherited motifs to Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma

questions.question_arabic: قُتِلَ الشَّاعِرُ دُونَ الثَّلَاثِينَ مِنْ عُمْرِهِ وَكَانَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الْمُعَلَّقَاتِ السَّبْعِ:
questions.question_english: He was put to death before the age of thirty and was among the poets of the Seven Mu'allaqat:
questions.explanation_arabic: قتل طرفة بن العبد البكري في البحرين بأمر ملك الحيرة عمرو بن هند وهو في نحو السادسة والعشرين من عمره، ولقب بـ 'ابن العشرين'.
questions.explanation_english: Tarafah ibn al-Abd was put to death in Bahrain at the age of twenty-six by order of King Amr ibn Hind, nicknamed 'Ibn al-Ishrin'.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَقْتَلُ الشَّاعِرِ طَرَفَةَ بْنِ الْعَبْدِ فِي سِنِّ السَّادِسَةِ وَالْعِشْرِينَ بِأَمْرِ عَمْرِو بْنِ هِنْدٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Execution of Tarafah ibn al-Abd at age 26 by order of Amr ibn Hind

questions.question_arabic: «إِذَا الْمَلِكُ الْجَبَّارُ صَعَّرَ خَدَّهُ ... مَشَيْنَا إِلَيْهِ بِالسُّيُوفِ نُعَاتِبُهْ»، قَالَهُ:
questions.question_english: "When a tyrannical king turns his cheek in haughty pride, we march toward him with swords to reprimand him." Said by:
questions.explanation_arabic: هذا البيت من روائع الفخر القبلي والسيادي لعمرو بن كلثوم التغلبي في تحدي الملوك والجبابرة.
questions.explanation_english: This famous martial verse defying tyrannical kings is from the proud poetry of Amr ibn Kulthum al-Taghlibi.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ التَّحَدِّي لِلْمُلُوكِ إِلَى الشَّاعِرِ الْفَارِسِ عَمْرِو بْنِ كُلْثُومٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of this defiant verse against tyrannical monarchs to Amr ibn Kulthum

questions.question_arabic: هُوَ مِنْ عُلَمَاءِ الدِّينِ الْإِسْلَامِيِّ وُلِدَ فِي الْقَلَمُونِ فِي لُبْنَانَ، مِنْ مُفَسِّرِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ (تَفْسِيرِ الْمَنَارِ)، هُوَ:
questions.question_english: He is an Islamic scholar born in al-Qalamoun in Lebanon, and one of the exegesis scholars of the Holy Qur'an:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَرْجَمَةُ مُحَمَّد رَشِيد رِضَا مُؤَسِّسِ مَجَلَّةِ الْمَنَارِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Biography of scholar Muhammad Rashid Rida and his birthplace

questions.question_arabic: مَجْمُوعَةُ مَقَالَاتِ الرَّافِعِيِّ الْأَدَبِيَّةِ وَالْإِسْلَامِيَّةِ الشَّهِيرَةِ:
questions.question_english: The famous collection of essays by al-Rafi'i is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: كِتَابُ وَحْيِ الْقَلَمِ لِمُصْطَفَى صَادِق الرَّافِعِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Rafi'i's essay collection Wahy al-Qalam

questions.question_arabic: امْتَازَ امْرُؤُ الْقَيْسِ بَيْنَ أَصْحَابِ الْمُعَلَّقَاتِ بِتَعَمُّقِهِ فِي مَعْرِفَةِ خَصَائِصِ النِّسَاءِ:
questions.question_english: Imru' al-Qais stood out among the Mu'allaqat poets for his profound psychological insight into the temperament and nature of women:
questions.explanation_arabic: أجمع النقاد أن امرأ القيس كان أسبق الشعراء إلى كشف مشاعر المرأة وخوالجها النفسية وسلوكها في مواقف العشق والدلال.
questions.explanation_english: Classical and modern critics note that Imru' al-Qais exhibited unmatched psychological insight into feminine psychology and courtship.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمَيُّزُ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ بِالْفَهْمِ النَّفْسِيِّ وَالتَّصْوِيرِ الدَّقِيقِ لِعَوَاطِفِ الْمَرْأَةِ فِي غَزَلِهِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Imru' al-Qais's psychological insight into feminine emotions in his erotic verses

questions.question_arabic: لَيْسَ مِنْ أَشْهَرِ الْمَدَّاحِينَ الْمُحْتَرِفِينَ فِي الْعَصْرِ الْجَاهِلِيِّ:
questions.question_english: Who among the following was not considered primarily a professional praise/panegyric poet in the Pre-Islamic era (his poetry being dominated by pride, passion, and personal quest):
questions.explanation_arabic: كان امرؤ القيس ملكاً ضليلاً ترفع عن التكسب بالشعر، بينما احترف النابغة والأعشى وزهير مدح الملوك وسادات القبائل كالغساسنة والمناذرة وهرم بن سنان.
questions.explanation_english: Imru' al-Qais was a prince who never composed panegyrics for reward, unlike professional praise poets such as al-Nabighah, al-A'sha, and Zuhayr.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ كَشَاعِرِ مُلْكٍ وَغَزَلٍ وَمُغَامَرَةٍ لَا يَتَكَسَّبُ بِالْمَدِيحِ كَالنَّابِغَةِ وَالْأَعْشَى وَزُهَيْرٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Distinguishing Imru' al-Qais as a prince who did not seek livelihood through panegyric

questions.question_arabic: «الْحَوْلِيَّاتُ» هِيَ قَصَائِدُ كَانَ يُنَقِّحُهَا الشَّاعِرُ فِي حَوْلٍ كَامِلٍ (سَنَةٍ)، وَهِيَ مَنْسُوبَةٌ إِلَى الشَّاعِرِ:
questions.question_english: "Al-Hawliyyat" (Annual Odes) were masterfully crafted poems refined over an entire year, attributed to:
questions.explanation_arabic: اشتهر زهير بن أبي سلمى بـ 'الحوليات'؛ حيث كان ينظم القصيدة في أربعة أشهر، ويهذبها في أربعة أشهر، ويعرضها على خواصه في أربعة أشهر ثم يخرجها للناس.
questions.explanation_english: Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma was celebrated for his 'Hawliyyat'—poems crafted, refined, and vetted over an entire four-stage yearly cycle.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ حَوْلِيَّاتِ زُهَيْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلْمَى فِي تَنْقِيحِ الْقَصِيدَةِ عَلَى مَدَارِ عَامٍ كَامِلٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma's Hawliyyat composed over a four-stage annual cycle

questions.question_arabic:
«وَإِذَا صَحَوْتُ فَلَا أُقَصِّرُ عَنْ نَدَى *** وَكَمَا عَلِمْتِ شَمَائِلِي وَتَكَرُّمِي»
قَالَهُ :
questions.question_english: In the verse: 'And when I sober up, I do not fall short in generosity, and as you well know, noble is my character and benevolence.' It was composed by:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ «وَإِذَا صَحَوْتُ فَلَا أُقَصِّرُ عَنْ نَدَى» لِعَنْتَرَةَ بْنِ شَدَّادٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the verse on generosity and sobriety to Antarah ibn Shaddad

questions.question_arabic: يَقَعُ شَطُّ الْعَرَبِ فِي :
questions.question_english: Shatt al-Arab is located in:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَوْقِعُ شَطِّ الْعَرَبِ الْجُغْرَافِيُّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The geographical location of Shatt al-Arab

questions.question_arabic: الشَّاعِرُ الَّذِي قَتَلَ مَلِكَ حِيرَةَ عَمْرَو بْنَ هِنْدٍ :
questions.question_english: The poet who killed the King of al-Hirah, Amr ibn Hind, is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: قَتْلُ عَمْرِو بْنِ كُلْثُومٍ لِمَلِكِ الْحِيرَةِ عَمْرِو بْنِ هِنْدٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Amr ibn Kulthum's killing of the King of al-Hirah Amr ibn Hind

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Locating the city of Ashkelon in historical Palestine

questions.question_arabic: عَنْتَرَةُ بْنُ عَمْرِو بْنِ شَدَّادٍ كَانَ مِنْ قَبِيلَةِ:
questions.question_english: Antarah ibn Amr ibn Shaddad belonged to the tribe of:
questions.explanation_arabic: عنترة بن شداد العبسي هو فارس وشاعر قبيلة بني عبس المضرية المشهورة.
questions.explanation_english: Antarah ibn Shaddad was the champion knight and poet of the Banu Abs tribe.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نَسَبُ الشَّاعِرِ عَنْتَرَةَ بْنِ شَدَّادٍ إِلَى قَبِيلَةِ عَبْسٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Lineage of poet Antarah ibn Shaddad to the tribe of Abs

عَلَيَّ بِأَنْوَاعِ الْهُمُومِ لِيَبْتَلِي
فِي هَذَا الشِّعْرِ يَشْتَرِكُ اللَّيْلُ وَ مَوْجُ الْبَحْرِ فِي صِفَتَيْنِ، هُمَا :
questions.question_english:
"And a night like a wave of the sea let down its curtains

In this verse, the night and the wave of the sea share two attributes, which are:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: وَجْهُ الشَّبَهِ بَيْنَ اللَّيْلِ وَمَوْجِ الْبَحْرِ فِي مُعَلَّقَةِ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The point of resemblance (wajh al-shabah) between night and sea wave in the Mu'allaqah of Imru' al-Qays

questions.question_english: Identify the incorrect author-book pairing among the following:

questions.correct_answer_text_arabic: ابْنُ قُتَيْبَةَ — كِتَابُ الْعَرَبِ وَالْمَوَالِي (لِلْجَاحِظِ / أَبِي عُبَيْدَةَ)

questions.explanation_arabic: كتاب العرب والموالي (أو تفضيل البطن على الظهر) من رسائل الجاحظ؛ أما ابن قتيبة فألف عيون الأخبار والشعر والشعراء وأدب الكاتب.
questions.explanation_english: 'Kitab al-Arab wa al-Mawali' was composed by al-Jahiz as part of his social epistles, not by Ibn Qutaybah.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَصْحِيحُ نِسْبَةِ رَسَائِلِ الْعَرَبِ وَالْمَوَالِي إِلَى أَبِي عُثْمَانَ الْجَاحِظِ وَلَيْسَ ابْنِ قُتَيْبَةَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Correcting attribution of 'Kitab al-Arab wa al-Mawali' to al-Jahiz rather than Ibn Qutaybah

questions.question_arabic: مَنْ هُوَ الْمَلِكُ الضِّلِّيلُ:
questions.question_english: Who is known by the title 'Al-Malik al-Dillil' (The Wandering/Errant King)?
questions.explanation_arabic: لُقب امرؤ القيس بن حجر الكندي بالملك الضليل وذي القروح لتشرده ومحاولته استرداد ملك أبيه حجر ملك كندة.
questions.explanation_english: Imru' al-Qais was titled 'Al-Malik al-Dillil' (The Wandering King) due to his exile seeking vengeance for his father.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: لَقَبُ «الْمَلِكِ الضِّلِّيلِ» لِامْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ الْكِنْدِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The title 'Al-Malik al-Dillil' for Imru' al-Qais al-Kindi

questions.question_arabic: عَاصِمَةُ الْإِمَارَاتِ الْمُتَّحِدَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ :
questions.question_english: The capital of the United Arab Emirates is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: عَاصِمَةُ دَوْلَةِ الْإِمَارَاتِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ الْمُتَّحِدَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The capital city of the United Arab Emirates (Abu Dhabi)

questions.correct_answer_text_english: Pure Arab (from Banu Haram of Rabi'ah)

questions.explanation_english: Al-Hariri was of pure Arab descent, belonging to the Banu Haram tribe established in Basra.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: الْأَصْلُ الْعَرَبِيُّ الْقَحُّ لِلْحَرِيرِيِّ صَاحِبِ الْمَقَامَاتِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Pure Arab tribal descent of al-Hariri, author of the Maqamat

questions.question_english: The most famous market of the Arabs in the Pre-Islamic period is:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَشْهَرُ أَسْوَاقِ الْعَرَبِ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ (سُوقُ عُكَاظٍ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: The most famous Arab market in the Pre-Islamic period (Suq Ukaz)

questions.explanation_arabic: عبد الحميد بن يحيى الكاتب كان من أهل الأنبار بالعراق ومولى لقريش، وتنقل معلماً للصبية حتى صار رئيس ديوان رسائل بني أمية.
questions.explanation_english: Abd al-Hamid ibn Yahya al-Katib was a native of al-Anbar in Iraq before rising to head the Umayyad imperial chancery.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: أَصْلُ وَنَشْأَةُ عَبْدِ الْحَمِيدِ الْكَاتِبِ فِي مَدِينَةِ الْأَنْبَارِ بِالْعِرَاقِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Birthplace and origins of Abd al-Hamid al-Katib in al-Anbar, Iraq

questions.question_english: An Egyptian Islamic scholar and reformer who advocated renewal, author of 'Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah':

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Author of Sharh Nahj al-Balaghah, Imam Muhammad Abduh

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the Mu'allaqah poet Antarah ibn Shaddad

questions.question_english: The Mu'allaqat are Pre-Islamic odes whose hanging on the Ka'bah was denied by many without established evidence, among them:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: إِنْكَارُ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ النَّحَّاسِ لِقِصَّةِ تَعْلِيقِ الْمُعَلَّقَاتِ عَلَى الْكَعْبَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas's denial of the physical hanging of the Muallaqat on the Ka'bah

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-A'sha as the first poet to make poetry a profession for wealth

questions.question_arabic: الْأَدِيبُ وَالصَّحَفِيُّ الْمِصْرِيُّ الْحَدِيثُ الَّذِي اشْتَرَكَ فِي تَحْرِيرِ الْأَهْرَامِ وَالْمُؤَيَّدِ وَالْمُقَطَّمِ:
questions.question_english: The modern Egyptian journalist who contributed to editing Al-Ahram, Al-Mu'ayyad, and Al-Muqattam:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: إِسْهَامَاتُ مُصْطَفَى كَامِل فِي الصِّحَافَةِ الْمِصْرِيَّةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Mustafa Kamil's contributions to Egyptian journalism

questions.question_english: A great pre-Islamic poet who died eleven years before the Hijrah, whose sons (Ka'b and Bujayr) embraced Islam:
questions.explanation_arabic: زهير بن أبي سلمى حكيم شعراء الجاهلية توفي قبل البعثة بقليل، وأدرك ولداه كعب وبجير الإسلام فأسلما.
questions.explanation_english: Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma died shortly before the Islamic call; his two sons Ka'b and Bujayr later accepted Islam.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَرْجَمَةُ زُهَيْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلْمَى وَإِسْلَامُ ابْنَيْهِ كَعْبٍ وَبُجَيْرٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Biography of Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma and the conversion of his sons Ka'b and Bujayr

questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: بَانِي جَامِعِ الْأَزْهَرِ الشَّرِيفِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Builder of Al-Azhar Mosque

questions.question_english: A Jahili poet born in Najd and died in Ankara, author of the first Mu'allaqah 'Stop, let us weep from the memory of a beloved and an abode, at the dune's edge between al-Dakhul and Hawmal':
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَرْجَمَةُ امْرِئِ الْقَيْسِ صَاحِبِ الْمُعَلَّقَةِ الْأُولَى
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Biography of Imru' al-Qais, author of the first Mu'allaqah

questions.question_english: The White Sea (Al-Bahr al-Abyad) is commonly known in geography as:
questions.explanation_arabic: يطلق العرب على البحر المتوسط اسم 'البحر الأبيض المتوسط' لتمييزه عن بحر القلزم (البحر الأحمر) والبحر الأسود.
questions.explanation_english: In Arabic geography, the Mediterranean Sea is referred to as Al-Bahr al-Abyad al-Mutawassit.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ تَسْمِيَةِ الْبَحْرِ الْأَبْيَضِ الْمُتَوَسِّطِ فِي الْعَالَمِ الْعَرَبِيِّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the Mediterranean Sea as the White Sea (Al-Bahr al-Abyad)

questions.question_arabic: قَائِلُ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: «لِسَانُ الْفَتَى نِصْفٌ وَنِصْفٌ فُؤَادُهُ / فَلَمْ يَبْقَ إِلَّا صُورَةُ اللَّحْمِ وَالدَّمِ»:

questions.explanation_arabic: هذا البيت من عيون أبيات الحكمة في ختام معلقة زهير بن أبي سلمى المزني.
questions.explanation_english: This verse is among the renowned aphorisms of wisdom concluded in Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma's Mu'allaqah.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ الْحِكْمَةِ الشَّهِيرِ إِلَى زُهَيْرِ بْنِ أَبِي سُلْمَى
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attributing the famous wisdom verse to Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma

questions.question_arabic: الْإِمَارَاتُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ الْمُتَّحِدَةُ تَتَكَوَّنُ مِنْ:

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Number of Emirates in the UAE

questions.question_english: Which of the following is not a work or poetry collection by Jamil Sidqi al-Zahawi:
questions.explanation_arabic: دواوين الزهاوي الشهيرة هي: الكلم المنظوم، اللباب، الأوشال، الثمالة، ونزغات الشيطان.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Zahawi's famous published diwans include 'Al-Lubab', 'Al-Awshal', and 'Al-Thumalah'.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ دَوَاوِينِ الزَّهَاوِي (اللُّبَاب، الْأَوْشَال، الثُّمَالَة، نَزَغَات الشَّيْطَان)

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Wandering of Imru' al-Qais with Arab outcasts after his father expelled him

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Meaning of the word sarhan in the Muallaqah of Imru' al-Qais

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Origin and residence of the critic Qudamah ibn Ja'far in Baghdad, Iraq

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Hafiz Ibrahim and Khalil Mutran's joint translation of Paul Leroy-Beaulieu's Political Economy

D.arabic: نَائِبُ رَئِيسِ مَجْلِسِ التَّرْجَمَةِ وَالتَّعْرِيبِ — مَعْرُوف الرُّصَافِي

questions.question_micro_focus_english: The author of 'Zu'ama al-Islah fi al-Asr al-Hadith'

questions.explanation_english: Al-Akhtal disparaged the Ansar in his political satire by mocking their date-farming and agrarian traditions.

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Al-Akhtal's taunts against the Ansar for their agrarian background in Medina

questions.question_arabic: مِنْ كِبَارِ شُعَرَاءِ الْعَرَبِ امْتَدَحَ سَيْفَ الدَّوْلَةِ :
questions.question_english: Among the greatest Arabic poets, renowned for praising Sayf al-Dawlah:

questions.question_micro_focus_english: The greatest Arab poet and his eulogies for Sayf al-Dawlah al-Hamdani (al-Mutanabbi)

questions.question_english: Jarir engaged in poetic duels and defeated contemporary poets numbering around:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: عَدَدُ الشُّعَرَاءِ الَّذِينَ هَجَاهُمْ جَرِيرٌ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Number of poets satirized and rivaled by Jarir

questions.question_arabic: مَنِ الْقَائِلُ : «تَرَى كُلَّ مَظْلُومٍ إِلَيْنَا قَرَارَهُ *** وَيَهْرُبُ مِنَّا جُهْدَهُ كُلُّ ظَالِمِ» :
questions.question_english: Who said the verse: 'You see every oppressed one seeking shelter with us, while every oppressor flees from us with all his might'?
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ «تَرَى كُلَّ مَظْلُومٍ إِلَيْنَا قَرَارَهُ» لِلْفَرَزْدَقِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the verse 'You see every oppressed one...' to Al-Farazdaq

questions.question_arabic: تَوَلَّى الْأَدِيبُ يَحْيَى حَقِّي رِئَاسَةَ تَحْرِيرِ مَجَلَّةٍ شَهْرِيَّةٍ ثَقَافِيَّةٍ رَائِدَةٍ هِيَ:
questions.question_english: The literary master Yahya Haqqi served as chief editor of the leading cultural monthly review:
questions.explanation_arabic: تولى يحيى حقي رئاسة تحرير مجلة 'المجلة' الصادرة عن وزارة الثقافة المصرية وجعلها منارة لرعاية جيل الستينيات الأدبي.
questions.explanation_english: Yahya Haqqi served as chief editor of 'Al-Majallah' from 1962 to 1970, nurturing a brilliant generation of modern Arab writers.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: رِئَاسَةُ يَحْيَى حَقِّي لِمَجَلَّةِ «الْمَجَلَّةِ» الْقَاهِرِيَّةِ لِثَمَانِي سَنَوَاتٍ (1962–1970 م)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Yahya Haqqi's eight-year stewardship of 'Al-Majallah' monthly

questions.question_arabic: «اذْهَبْ إِلَى أَبِي بَكْرٍ فَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِمَثَالِبِ الْقَوْمِ» قَالَهُ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لِـ:
questions.question_english: 'Go to Abu Bakr, for he is the most knowledgeable regarding the genealogies and faults of the people.' Said by the Prophet (pbuh) to:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَوْجِيهُ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ لِحَسَّانَ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ لِأَخْذِ أَنْسَابِ قُرَيْشٍ مِنْ أَبِي بَكْرٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Hassan ibn Thabit learning Qurayshite genealogies from Abu Bakr

questions.question_arabic: اسْمُ الْأَعْشَى الْكَامِلُ:
questions.question_english: The full name of the pre-Islamic poet Al-A'sha is:
questions.explanation_arabic: الأعشى الكبير (صناجة العرب) اسمه ميمون بن قيس بن جندل البكري وهو أحد أصحاب المعلقات.
questions.explanation_english: Al-A'sha, known as Sanajat al-Arab (The Cymbalist of the Arabs), was named Maymun ibn Qays al-Bakri.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ الِاسْمِ الْكَامِلِ لِلشَّاعِرِ الْأَعْشَى (مَيْمُونِ بْنِ قَيْسٍ)
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Knowledge of the full name of poet Al-A'sha (Maymun ibn Qays)

questions.question_arabic: لِأَوَّلِ مَرَّةٍ جُمِعَ الْقُرْآنُ الْكَرِيمُ مِنَ السُّطُورِ وَالصُّدُورِ فِي عَهْدِ الْخَلِيفَةِ:
questions.question_english: For the first time, the Holy Quran was systematically assembled into a single comprehensive manuscript under:

A.arabic: أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
A.english: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)

B.arabic: عُمَرَ بْنِ الْخَطَّابِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

C.arabic: عُثْمَانَ بْنِ عَفَّانَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

D.arabic: زَيْدِ بْنِ ثَابِتٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ

questions.correct_answer_text_arabic: أَبِي بَكْرٍ الصِّدِّيقِ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ
questions.correct_answer_text_english: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him)
questions.explanation_arabic: أمر أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه بجمع القرآن الكريم بعد استشهاد عدد كبير من حفظة القرآن في معركة اليمامة وأوكل المهمة لزيد بن ثابت.
questions.explanation_english: Caliph Abu Bakr ordered the first unified compilation of the Quran following the martyrdom of numerous Quranic memorizers at Yamamah.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: جَمْعُ الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيمِ فِي مُصْحَفٍ وَاحِدٍ فِي خِلَافَةِ الصِّدِّيقِ بَعْدَ حَرْبِ الْيَمَامَةِ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: First compilation of the Quran under Abu Bakr following the Battle of Yamamah

questions.question_arabic: مِنَ الشُّعَرَاءِ الْفُرْسَانِ فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ:
questions.question_english: Among the renowned knight-poets (Al-Shu'ara' al-Fursan) in the Pre-Islamic era:
questions.explanation_arabic: عنترة بن شداد العبسي هو أشهر فرسان العرب وشعرائهم أصحاب المعلقات وفارس بني عبس الذي ارتبط اسمه بالفروسية.
questions.explanation_english: Antarah ibn Shaddad al-Absi is celebrated as the archetype of Arab chivalric knight-poets.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَمْيِيزُ عَنْتَرَةَ بْنِ شَدَّادٍ الْعَبْسِيِّ كَأَشْهَرِ فُرْسَانِ الْعَرَبِ وَشُعَرَائِهِمْ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying Antarah ibn Shaddad as the quintessential Pre-Islamic knight-poet

questions.question_arabic: الْأَخْطَلُ كَانَ يَدِينُ بِـ:
questions.question_english: Al-Akhtal adhered to the religious faith of:
questions.explanation_arabic: الأخطل (غياث بن غوث التغلبي) كان مسيحياً تغلبيّاً وظل على نصرانيته ومات عليها وكان شاعر بلاط بني أمية.
questions.explanation_english: Al-Akhtal (Ghiyath ibn Ghawth) was a Christian poet of the Taghlib tribe who served as the official court poet of the Umayyads.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَعْرِفَةُ دِيَانَةِ الشَّاعِرِ الْأُمَوِيِّ الْأَخْطَلِ كَنَصْرَانِيٍّ مِنْ بَنِي تَغْلِبَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying al-Akhtal as a Christian Arab poet of Banu Taghlib

questions.question_arabic: تُوُفِّيَ الشَّاعِرُ عُمَرُ أَبُو رِيشَةَ فِي مَدِينَةِ :
questions.question_english: The poet Omar Abu Risha passed away in the city of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: مَكَانُ وَفَاةِ الشَّاعِرِ عُمَرَ أَبِي رِيشَةَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Place of death of Omar Abu Risha

questions.question_arabic:
«نَقِّلْ فُؤَادَكَ حَيْثُ شِئْتَ مِنَ الْهَوَى *** مَا الْحُبُّ إِلَّا لِلْحَبِيبِ الْأَوَّلِ»
مِنْ شِعْرِ :
questions.question_english: In the verse: 'Turn your heart wherever you wish in passion, true love belongs only to the first beloved.' This is from the poetry of:
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: نِسْبَةُ بَيْتِ «نَقِّلْ فُؤَادَكَ حَيْثُ شِئْتَ مِنَ الْهَوَى» لِأَبِي تَمَّامٍ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Attribution of the famous verse on first love to Abu Tammam

questions.question_english: The celebrated hero and warrior-poet of the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah:
questions.explanation_arabic: عمرو بن معديكرب الزبيدي فارس اليمن وشاعرها المخضرم وأحد أبطال معركة القادسية ضد الفرس.
questions.explanation_english: Amr ibn Ma'dikarib al-Zubaydi was the legendary Yemeni champion and warrior-poet at the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: تَحْدِيدُ بَطَلِ مَعْرَكَةِ الْقَادِسِيَّةِ عَمْرِو بْنِ مَعْدِيكَرِبَ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Identifying the hero of the Battle of al-Qadisiyyah, Amr ibn Ma'dikarib

questions.question_english: Abu Ubadah al-Walid ibn Ubayd ibn Yahya is the poet:

questions.question_micro_focus_english: Full name of the poet al-Buhturi

questions.question_english: A female writer who lived in Egypt, mastered Arabic and Western culture, and hosted a famous Tuesday literary salon:
questions.explanation_arabic: مي زيادة أديبة نابغة أقامت صالونها الأدبي الأسبوعي في القاهرة الذي ضم كبار أعلام العصر كالعقاد ولطفي السيد وطه حسين.
questions.explanation_english: Mayy Ziyadah hosted Cairo's pre-eminent literary salon attended by leading figures such as Al-Aqqad and Taha Hussein.
questions.question_micro_focus_arabic: دَوْرُ مَيّ زِيَادَةَ فِي النَّهْضَةِ الْأَدَبِيَّةِ وَصَالُونُهَا الثُّلَاثَائِيُّ
questions.question_micro_focus_english: Mayy Ziyadah's role in the literary renaissance and her Tuesday salon
